concepts.description:
A Pop’s Acceptance is a value from … to …, which determines which Acceptance Status the Pop has.

Acceptance is primarily determined by the Pop’s Culture and Religion, and the corresponding … and … Law Groups in the Country the Pop lives in.

Acceptance changes are not always instant; Pops of a certain Cultural Community may have a different Acceptance, due to recent Law changes or Immigration.
concepts.name: Acceptance

concepts.description:
A Pop’s Acceptance Status determines how accepted or discriminated it is in a Country.

The Status a Pop gets is determined by its Acceptance value.

The exact effects of a certain Acceptance Status are determined by the Country’s Laws.

Possible Acceptance Statuses are, from lowest to highest:
• …
• …
• …
• …
• …
concepts.name: Acceptance Status

concepts.description: A Country’s Accepted Cultures consist of its Primary Cultures, plus any other Cultures considered Accepted due to the Country's current … Law. Usually, the two highest statuses of Acceptance are considered to be Accepted.
concepts.name: Accepted Culture

concepts.description: A Country’s Accepted Religions consist of its State Religion, plus any other Religions considered Accepted due to the Country's current … Law.
concepts.name: Accepted Religion

concepts.description: An increase or decrease to the probability that the Ship will hit when attacking
concepts.name: Accuracy

concepts.description: Expenses that don't fit into another category, often incurred due to the outcome of special events.
concepts.name: Additional Expenses

concepts.description: Income that doesn't fit into another category, often gained from the outcome of special events.
concepts.name: Additional Income

concepts.description: A naval Commander Character who leads a Country’s Ships. Effects from an Admiral's Character Traits are conferred onto Ships under their command.
concepts.name: Admiral

concepts.description: Advance Factor is a static factor used to determine Enactment Advance by scaling the Base Success chance.
concepts.name: Advance Factor

concepts.description: Generals Ordered to advance a Front accumulate Advancement Progress daily depending on their Advancement Speed. Once the Advancement Progress of the Front has reached … a Battle will start. While a Battle is ongoing on the Front, Advancement Progress on that Front will be paused.
concepts.name: Advancement Progress

concepts.description:
How rapidly a General can advance their Front by accumulating Advancement Progress.
A General with no Mobilized Battalions has an effective Advancement Speed of zero.
concepts.name: Advancement Speed

concepts.description:
A Role for Characters who support a Political Movement, making it more attractive to Individuals belonging to their Interest Group. Agitators may be invited with the Invite Exile character action or will appear randomly in your country, with their chance of appearance dependent upon your Country's Literacy.

Agitators can only be invited if their Acceptance Status is one of the following in your Country: … or ….

The Political Movement they support is determined by their Ideology. Their impact on their Political Movement is determined by the Agitator's Popularity and Character Traits.
concepts.name: Agitator

concepts.description:
A Stance is an indication of a Countries foreign policy views within a specific Strategic Region.

This can affect how a Country reacts to a Diplomatic Play or whether it wants to launch one itself, as well as the Attitude that it develops towards Countries in that Region.
concepts.name: AI Strategic Region Stance

concepts.description: Alerts that appear as their own individual element with an icon to the right of the Capacities and Current Situation at the top center of the screen.
concepts.name: Alert

concepts.description: A Treaty Article between two Countries. Countries engaged in an Alliance may always side with each other in Diplomatic Plays regardless of if the other side maintains an Interest in the affected Strategic Region. This applies no matter if the other Country is the initiator or target of the Play.
concepts.name: Alliance

concepts.description:
Determines which Countries are affected by the Strait Access restrictions if it is set to No Military or Closed

The Allowed Countries can be set to:
No enemies
Access restrictions only affects Ships from enemies of the Strait Controller

Only allies
Only Ships of allies to the Strait Controller are exempt from the restrictions

Only Controller
Only Ships from the Strait Controller & its Subjects are exempt from the restrictions
concepts.name: Allowed Countries

concepts.description: An Ally is a Country which maintains an Alliance or Defensive Pact with another country and can be called to support them in Diplomatic Plays. For the Initiator, only Countries with a full Alliance are considered to be Allies in that Diplomatic Play.
concepts.name: Ally

concepts.description:
How willing an Interest Group is to Negotiate during the Enactment of Laws, higher value means more willing.

0 - …:     Will refuse to Negotiate
… - …:   Tense
… - …:   Pragmatic
… - 100: Collaborative
concepts.name: Amenability

concepts.description: An Amendment is an addition to a Law that alters its effects, sponsored by a specific Interest Group. If an Interest will Endorse or Oppose an Amendment is determined by the Parent Law of the Amendment. An Amendment may be Repealed if the Amendment is not on cooldown, and any Interest Group in Government Opposes the Amendment's Parent Law.
concepts.name: Amendment

concepts.description: An Amendment may be Repealed if the Amendment is not on cooldown, and any Interest Group in Government Opposes the Amendment's Parent Law.
concepts.name: Amendment Repeal

concepts.description: Red Alerts that appear in the list when you click the Current Situations button.
concepts.name: Angry Important Action

concepts.description:
The Appeasement of a Political Lobby affects the Approval of the Interest Groups of the Lobby.

Appeasement changes based on your Diplomatic Actions against the Lobby's Country. Pro-Lobbies are appeased by friendly Actions, while Anti-Lobbies are appeased by hostile Actions.
concepts.name: Appeasement

concepts.description:
An Interest Group’s Approval depends on two main factors: how much of their Political Strength comes from Radicals compared to Loyalists, and how well the Country’s current Laws match with the Interest Group's Ideologies. In addition, if a new Law is currently being Enacted, Approval will be affected by a larger temporary adjustment which will linger while Decaying for up to … months after it has passed.

An Interest Group's Approval impacts which Interest Group Traits they activate. … Interest Groups contribute to the Activism of Political Movements, while Interest Groups that are at least … will refrain from joining Movements in the first place. An Interest Group with Approval at or below … may launch a Coup against the sitting Government.
concepts.name: Approval

concepts.description:
The amount of land in a State that can be used for cultivating crops or raising cattle. Unlike Buildings that require certain Resource Potentials to be constructed, Arable Land must be shared between the Building types that require it.

The amount of Arable Land that stands unused by other Buildings may be used for Subsistence Buildings, letting Pops eke out a meager living even if not gainfully employed.
concepts.name: Arable Land

concepts.description:
An Army is a land Formation composed of Infantry, Artillery and Cavalry Battalions, led by a General who lends bonuses from his Character Traits and Orders to the whole Army.

When deployed to a Front, an Army executes its Order such as Advance Front or Defend Front, fighting Battles against any enemy Armies present on that Front. How well it fights depends on the Offense and Defense of its Battalions and their Morale.

An Army must be ordered to Mobilize before its Battalions are ready to fight, and stands down again automatically once the War ends. Before Mobilizing, the Army can be configured with Mobilization Options that apply effects to its Battalions at a cost of Goods while Mobilized.
concepts.name: Army

concepts.description: The Power Projection derived from a Country’s army.
concepts.name: Army Power Projection

concepts.description:
Articles are the components that make up a Treaty and can take many shapes.

An Article can apply several effects upon one or both Countries involved and will usually incur an Influence cost for as long as the Treaty is upheld, alternatively an Article may also apply specific one-time effects or impart certain duties upon the responsible Country that may negatively affect the Treaty if Contravened where the Treaty may eventually become Non-Fulfilled.

Each Article falls under one of two categories:
• Mutual: Mutual Articles extend all of their effects and duties to both Countries equally.
• Directional: Directional Articles have different effects and duties towards one or the other Country depending one whether they are the offering or receiving side respectively.
concepts.name: Article

concepts.description: Foreign Pops whose Culture has high enough Acceptance in the Country they live in, and who do not live in one of their Homelands, may Assimilate into a more Accepted Culture. Pops that contain Radicals will assimilate at a reduced rate, and Assimilation is much slower in Unincorporated States.
concepts.name: Assimilation

concepts.description: An increase or decrease to the amount of damage a Ship can deal to another Ship’s hull
concepts.name: Attack Damage

concepts.description:
An indication of how another Country feels about you.

Attitude affects what sorts of actions a Country is likely to take towards you, and what role you play in their plans.

Attitude may change whenever a Diplomatic Catalyst occurs, and is based on:
• Relations
• Infamy
• Strategic Desire
• Size of your military
• Which Countries you have Diplomatic Pacts with
concepts.name: Attitude

concepts.description: Casualties inflicted on Manpower outside of Battle is referred to as Attrition. It is frequently experienced when Battalions are Mobilized and can be the result of disease, accidents, exposure, or even desertion. Attrition can be counteracted by using Medical Support Mobilization Options.
concepts.name: Attrition

concepts.description: Authority is a Capacity used to effect internal change to your Country, like issuing Decrees or managing Interest Groups. You gain from Laws.
concepts.name: Authority

concepts.description:
Each Subject Country has its own Autonomy level. This level will determine what kind of interaction they will have with their Overlord.

A Subject with high Autonomy will be more independent in regards to diplomacy. They will also have lower tribute payments to their Overlord. There is a risk that a Country that is too Autonomous will attempt to Declare an Independence Diplomatic Play.
Subjects with low Autonomy will be more reliant on their Overlords and pay larger tributes to their Overlord. Subjects with the lowest level of Autonomy can be integrated with a Annex Subject Diplomatic Play into their Overlord.
concepts.name: Autonomy

concepts.description: A Country’s available Battalions include all Battalions currently raised by … and/or Conscription Centers.
concepts.name: Available Battalions

concepts.description: The average Wages a single Individual in the Workforce would earn annually while working at this Building.
concepts.name: Average Annual Wage

concepts.description:
A Building’s Balance is the amount of Money that remains of its Revenue after paying Wages and purchasing required Input Goods.

The Balance is divided between Building Owners and the Building's Cash Reserves.

A Building's Balance can be improved either by making its Input Goods cheaper, or by making its Output Goods more expensive. This can be done by increasing or decreasing Supply and Demand on the Market it belongs to.
concepts.name: Balance

concepts.description:
Secessionist Political Movements driven by the following Cultures impact Rumelian Integrity: 
• …
• …
• …
• …
• …
• …
• …
concepts.name: Balkan Culture

concepts.description: One Country pays part of its income to another, based on the weekly tax revenue of the recipient. This action has a chance each month to generate an Obligation towards the bankrolling Country so long as it was not given as part of a Sway offer.
concepts.name: Bankroll

concepts.description: If a Country is in Default and unable to pay back its Loans, it may opt to declare Bankruptcy. This will clear the debt but wipe out all Cash Reserves the Country had borrowed from, and will greatly anger any Pops who Privately Owns Buildings.…
concepts.name: Bankruptcy

concepts.description: The price of a Good when its Supply exactly equal its Demand.
concepts.name: Base Price

concepts.description: Base Success chance is equal to the total Clout of supporting Interest Groups in Government plus or minus Support gained from any relevant Political Movements.
concepts.name: Base Success chance

concepts.description: The original design of a Ship Type. The Base Template unlocks with the Ship Type and will always be available.
concepts.name: Base Template

concepts.description: An army Military Unit in a Country’s military. They are created and maintained by … and are commanded by Generals.
concepts.name: Battalion

concepts.description:
When two Commanders encounter each other and come into conflict during a War, they and their Military Units will clash in an attempt to inflict Casualties and damage each others' Morale. The side whose Manpower has run out or become Demoralized first will withdraw, leaving the other side victorious.

On land, Battles take place in Provinces adjacent to Fronts when one General is advancing to take or regain Land. The winner will either conquer more Provinces or prevent the enemy from doing so.
concepts.name: Battle

concepts.description: During Battles each side will be affected by a Battle Condition that influences the outcome. Which Condition applies depends on a number of factors, which often includes the Character Traits of the Commanders in charge of that side.
concepts.name: Battle Condition

concepts.description:
Ire represents the Greek population's opposition to the rule of the Bavarian clique in Greece. High Ire may result in the ousting of King Otto and his Bavarian supporters.

The following conditions will advance Ire:
• … Commanders or Characters in In Government
• Not having an … Ruler
• The Ruler Not having an Heir
• The Ruler being unmarried 
• Not having Voting Rights
• Fielding less than 10 Battalions
• Radicals in owned … Homeland States
• Having recently lost a War
• Event or button choices

The following conditions will deplete Ire:
• Owning … Homeland States
• Loyalists in owned … Homeland States
• Having recently won a War
• Having at least one … in a … Homeland State
• Fielding more than 20 Battalions
• Event or button choices
concepts.name: Bavarocratic Ire

concepts.description: A Treaty usually has a Binding Period where any withdrawal from the Treaty by either Country will result in penalties for the withdrawing Country. When the Binding Period has passed, withdrawal does not apply penalties anymore.
concepts.name: Binding Period

concepts.description: A type of Diplomatic Action that Bloc Leaders can issue against Bloc Members.
concepts.name: Bloc Leader Action

concepts.description: A type of Diplomatic Action that Bloc Members can issue against other Bloc Members, including the Bloc Leader.
concepts.name: Bloc Member Action

concepts.description: Blockades are a set up in a Sea Node via an Admiral Order. They damage Supply Networks and reduce access to the World Market in ports adjacent to the Sea Node. The Blockade Level is determined by the respective attribute on ship Military Unit. Capital Ships are best suited for Blockades.
concepts.name: Blockade

concepts.description: Blockade Efficiency is the average Blockade level a Fleet achieves across all hostile ports in its Naval Mission area. It is based on Blockade Strength vs the Blockade Resistance of each target port, distributed evenly across all targeted ports.
concepts.name: Blockade Efficiency

concepts.description: Blockade Resistance is the amount of Blockade Strength required to fully Blockade a State. It is based on factors such as Coastal Building output and local Trade volumes.
concepts.name: Blockade Resistance

concepts.description: Determines the degree to which a Fleet is able to successfully Blockade enemy States.
concepts.name: Blockade Strength

concepts.description: In Buddhism, an enlightened being and teacher who helps other attain nirvana.
concepts.name: Boddhisattva

concepts.description: A Bolstered Political Movement is more attractive for Pops to support. Your base Bolstering ability is determined by your … Law. Bolstering Interest Groups costs Authority.
concepts.name: Bolster

concepts.description:
Buildings drive your Country’s economy via the Production (and Consumption) of Goods. They can also produce a number of other useful effects, such as Bureaucracy, Infrastructure, and ….

To perform their functions they require a Workforce made up by Pops of different Professions, who receive a Wage in return for their labor.

What functions a particular Building serves is determined by its active Production Methods, and the magnitude of its impact is determined by its Level.…
concepts.name: Building

concepts.description:
A Building Group is a group of Buildings most often used to describe similar Buildings needed to fulfill certain conditions in, for example, Journal Entries.

Common Building Groups are:
• …
• …
• …
concepts.name: Building Group

concepts.description:
A Building’s Level scales its current Consumption, Production, Workforce requirements, and may apply an Economy of Scale bonus.

Expanding a Building's Level usually requires Construction, though some Building's Level is automatically adjusted based on other factors such as Infrastructure, Conscription rate, or unused Arable Land.

Each Level is either Privately Owned or Nationally Owned.

The maximum Level a Building can be expanded to may depend on the Resource Potential or Arable Land in the State.
concepts.name: Building Level

concepts.description: A Building’s size is divided into Levels. These Levels can either be Privately Owned by Pops, or Nationally Owned by a Country. The Profit from a Building is shared among its owners as Dividends.
concepts.name: Building Owners

concepts.description: Bureaucracy is a Capacity used to maintain your Country’s administrative cohesion and day-to-day operations. The cost increases with the population across your Incorporated States and with every Institution investment level, and is also used to administer Commanders. You gain from operating … Buildings.
concepts.name: Bureaucracy

concepts.description: A Character can be considered Busy when occupied with a certain assignment, such as being on an expedition. When Busy, the Character is unavailable for their regular duties. For example, a Commander would be unable to participate in Battles.
concepts.name: Busy

concepts.description: The number of orders to buy a Good on the central Market is used in combination with Sell Orders to determine its Market Price. Buy Orders are generated by the consumption of the Good in each of the Market's States. The higher the Market Access a State has, the closer the number of Buy Orders generated will be to the total consumption.
concepts.name: Buy Orders

concepts.description: A Canal is a Building that also includes the construction of an artificial connection between two sea nodes across a landmass. Canals can only be constructed in particular places and typically require the completion of some sort of survey or other expedition first. Canals can drastically shorten the distance … need to travel when establishing Shipping Lanes, making trade with distant lands more affordable.
concepts.name: Canal

concepts.description: A measure of your Country’s capabilities in one of three areas: Bureaucracy, Authority, and Influence. Capacities are not stored and used, but continuously generated from different sources and continually expended by the various projects you have going on. Your remaining balance in each area is displayed in the top bar. Having an excess of a Capacity will yield a minor bonus for your Country, while having a lack of a Capacity will inflict large penalties.
concepts.name: Capacity

concepts.description: The site of a Country’s central Government. Controlling the Capital is of great importance during wartime, and Pops who live there have a greater degree of Political Strength by which to influence politics.…
concepts.name: Capital State

concepts.description: An AI-controlled Country will try to capitulate if this value reaches 0 or higher.
concepts.name: Capitulation Desire

concepts.description: How many Battalions a single Ship can transport to support a Naval Invasion
concepts.name: Carrying Capacity

concepts.description:
The assets of a Building are stored in its Cash Reserves. If the Building runs a positive weekly Balance, some of the Money is deposited into the Cash Reserves while the rest is paid out to the Building Owners as Dividends.

Cash Reserves are considered to be owned by the Building Owners, and Pops will get angry if their Cash Reserves are lost due to Bankruptcy. The sum of all Cash Reserves in your Country determines your Credit.
concepts.name: Cash Reserves

concepts.description: Manpower who fall in battle or through Attrition are considered Casualties. A proportion of Casualties are killed outright while the remainder are Wounded. This ratio is dependent on the Military Unit’s Recovery Rate compared to their enemy's Kill Rate.
concepts.name: Casualties

concepts.description: The Central Identity Pillar defines the core values a Power Bloc revolves around. They determine the Power Bloc's Cohesion and grant special powers to the Power Bloc Leader. They can unlock certain Principle Groups.
concepts.name: Central Identity Pillar

concepts.description: As Liberty Desire nears either 0 or 100, its progress is slowed by Change Rate Scaling, reflecting a natural hesitance in the Population to depart from the status quo and accept increased or decreased Autonomy.
concepts.name: Change Rate Scaling

concepts.description: Characters fulfill different Roles in your Country. Their ability to perform these duties depends on their Character Traits. They always support an Interest Group, and may have an Ideology that shapes their aspirations and outlook.
concepts.name: Character

concepts.description: Personality Traits, Skill Traits, or Conditions that impact a Character’s ability to carry out their current Role. More or different Character Traits may develop as the Character gains Life Experience.
concepts.name: Character Trait

concepts.description: In special circumstances, Recognized Powers may establish a Chartered Company (Subject). A Chartered Company is a highly autonomous Subject Type that are able to start their own Diplomatic Plays and are forced to join their Overlord’s Wars. There are also special restrictions on reducing the Autonomy, and their base Liberty Desire gain is greatly reduced. They must pay 40% of their Treasury income to their Overlord each week.
concepts.name: Chartered Company

concepts.description: A War where a Country has split into two opposing sides. It can either be a Revolution or a Secession stemming from a Political Movement.
concepts.name: Civil War

concepts.description:
A territorial Claim that a Country has on a State Region, usually because it once belonged to them. Having a Claim permits use of the Return State War Goal which does not generate as much Infamy as the Conquer State War Goal does.

Conquering an Incorporated State will give the previous owner a Claim on the State Region.
concepts.name: Claim

concepts.description: An Interest Group’s share of the total Political Strength that Pops across their Country generate. Clout is the final word on how influential an Interest Group is, and affects everything from Legitimacy and Enactment of Laws if the Interest Group is In Government, to Political Movement Support and Activism if it is In Opposition. It also affects whether the Interest Group is considered Powerful, Influential, or Marginalized.
concepts.name: Clout

concepts.description:
A Coastal Building is a Building located in the port area of a coastal State. During a Blockade, non-military Coastal Buildings suffer reduced Throughput. … can destroy levels of any Coastal Building, including military ones.

There are a total of … Coastal Buildings:
…
concepts.name: Coastal Building

concepts.description: Cohesion is the indicator for how well a Power Bloc is running. It is mostly affected by the Central Identity Pillar which informs what impacts the value. The larger the Power Bloc, the lower the Cohesion will generally be.
concepts.name: Cohesion

concepts.description: A measure of how rapidly a Country can push the Colonial frontier forward. Colonial Growth is generated by the … Institution in combination with the total Population across Incorporated States. The total amount of Colonial Growth generated is split up across all Colonies a Country is actively growing, up to a maximum.…
concepts.name: Colonial Growth

concepts.description: A Diplomatic Pact that is created when a Decentralized Nation is defeated in a Native Uprising. It increases the speed at which the country granted Colonization Rights colonizes their territory, and lasts for the duration of the truce.
concepts.name: Colonization Rights

concepts.description: Settlement efforts initiated by a colonizing Country in the lands of a Decentralized Nation. A would-be colonizer must have the … Institution and an Interest in the Strategic Region. At first, a single Province will be taken. Adjacent Provinces will be Colonized at a rate depending on the Country's Colonial Growth, generating Tension as they do.
concepts.name: Colony

concepts.description: Recognized Powers may turn a weaker Country into their Colony (Subject). A Colony is a Subject Type that cannot start their own Diplomatic Plays yet are forced to join their Overlord’s Wars, and must also pay 30% of their Treasury income to their Overlord each week. A Colony's Rank cannot increase to match or exceed their Overlord's, and their Overlord may target them with the Annexation Diplomatic Play.
concepts.name: Colony

concepts.description: The Combat Width of a particular Terrain type influences the potential numeric advantage the larger side can have over the smaller side in Battle. A smaller force can hold out for longer against a larger force if Combat Width is relatively low, and vice versa.
concepts.name: Combat Width

concepts.description:
Command Limit determines how many Battalions or Ships can be effectively Organized under a Formation. You can increase Command Limit by promoting your Commander to a higher Commander Rank.

For an Army, whichever is higher of your regular Battalions or raised Conscript Battalions is compared against the Command Limit. This means raising Conscript Battalions will only strain the Command Limit if there are more of them than your regular Battalions.

Having more Military Units in a Formation than its Command Limit reduces the maximum Organization a Formation can reach, and additionally confers the following effects:
…
concepts.name: Command Limit

concepts.description: A Character in command of a Country’s Formation. A Commander can be either a General or an Admiral depending on the type of Formation they are leading. Their Commander Rank contributes to the Command Limit of the Formation they are in, and also impacts the amount of troops that they are able to bring with them into battle. Popular Commanders belonging to an Interest Group with low Approval may initiate a Coup.
concepts.name: Commander

concepts.description: A Commander’s Rank determines their Command Limit, as well as how much Clout they confer to their Interest Group. Retiring a Commander will cause their Interest Group's Approval to fall by a factor depending on their Rank.
concepts.name: Commander Rank

concepts.description:
Companies are associated with one or several types of Buildings in a Country. When established in said Country they increase the Throughput and …Construction efficiency of their associated Buildings. The degree to which a Company provides benefits depends on the relative Prestige ranking of the Country, with Countries in the Top-… receiving even stronger bonuses.

Companies have a Prosperity score which increases from high Productivity and can provide additional bonuses for its Country.
concepts.name: Company

concepts.description:
A Company Category describes which kinds of Pops partake in the ownership of a Company. It determines which Production Methods are available in the Company HQ, shaping which Professions are employed there. It also determines who receive a share of the Dividends, and whether the Company pays Government Dividends or not.

The Categories are:
Full Capitalist Ownership
Fully owned by …, who receive the full share of the Dividends.

Partial Aristocratic Ownership
Co-owned by … and …, who share the Dividends.

Partial Shopkeeper Ownership
Co-owned by … and …, with an extra share paid out as worker Dividends.

Partial Bureaucrat Ownership
Co-owned by … and …, with an extra share paid out as Government Dividends to the Treasury.

Partial Academic Ownership
Co-owned by … and …, with an extra share paid out as worker Dividends.
concepts.name: Company Category

concepts.description: Countries can give their Companies a Company Charter which grants the Company a particular right. These rights can range from establishing a Monopoly to the rights to build a different Industry or to construct a Regional Company HQ in another country. Countries have a number of free Company Charters they can hand out at no cost. Technologies and Laws can increase this limit. Additional Charters past the limit can be given to Companies, but will incur an Authority cost.
concepts.name: Company Charter

concepts.description: Company HQs are Buildings that represent the administration of Company assets. They own Building Levels from which they receive their Dividends.
concepts.name: Company HQ

concepts.description: A Company Monopoly gives a Company a Monopoly on a Building with exclusive Building rights of that Industry
concepts.name: Company Monopoly

concepts.description: An AI-controlled Country that is one of the main participants in a Diplomatic Play has a level of Confidence based on their internal conditions and how likely they believe it is that they will be able to win any ensuing war. The chance that the AI Country will decide to back down is directly determined by their confidence, though this is not guaranteed even at low Confidence levels, especially if backing down would lead to their annexation.
concepts.name: Confidence

concepts.description:
Conscript Battalions are temporary Battalions recruited and maintained from the civilian Population by Conscription Centers and activated during Diplomatic Plays or Wars.

Note that Conscript Battalions do not count towards the Command Limit of an Army until actually being raised and employed. When raised, only the higher of your regular Battalions or Conscript Battalions is compared against the Command Limit, so raising Conscript Battalions will only strain the limit if you have more of them than regular Battalions.
concepts.name: Conscript Battalion

concepts.description:
When a State is Conscripted during a Diplomatic Play or War, a … appears with a Building Level depending on its Conscription Rate and State Population size. This Military Building will recruit civilian Workforce into Conscript Battalions that will be automatically assigned to Generals in their HQ as they are raised.

After the War, all Conscription Centers will deactivate and the Conscript Battalions will disband. Pops who return to civilian life are not guaranteed to return to their old Profession but must seek new employment opportunities.
concepts.name: Conscription Center

concepts.description: The max number of Conscript Battalions a State can recruit. The Conscription Limit is calculated from the Workforce of a State multiplied by its Conscription Rate. It cannot exceed the Maximum Conscription Limit set in place by your … Law.
concepts.name: Conscription Limit

concepts.description:
Constitutional Pressure represents the strength and influence of the opposition to the neo-absolutist regime, and is tied to the preceived authority of the regime.

Should Constitutional Pressure reach 100, the neo-absolutist government will fall, and a constitution will be have to be granted. 

The following conditions increase Pressure: 
• Having a War Goal enforced on you
• Declaring Bankruptcy
• Taking Loans
• States with Radicals
• Interest Groups opposing …
• Activism of #tooltippable;tooltip:…,liberal_movements_list_tt Liberal, #tooltippable;tooltip:…,socialist_movements_list_tt Socialist, and National Political Movements
• Having a Bureaucracy deficit
• Events and other conditions 

The following conditions decrease Pressure: 
• Having a positive budget balance
• Enforcing a War Goal on a Great Power
• States with Loyalists
• Interest Groups supporting …
• Support of Absolutist, Religious Traditionalist, and Cultural Supremacist Political Movements
• Having a Bureaucracy surplus
• Events and other conditions
concepts.name: Constitutional Pressure

concepts.description: Construction is produced by the … and is used to construct Buildings.
concepts.name: Construction

concepts.description: Goods Consumed by … Buildings in order to Construct new Buildings.
concepts.name: Construction Goods

concepts.description: Any Buildings that have been set to be expanded, but are currently not using any Construction, are placed in the Construction Queue. Whenever any Construction becomes available, the first Building in the Construction Queue will start using that Construction and then switch to being Under Construction.
concepts.name: Construction Queue

concepts.description: The amount of a Good consumed by a Building or Pop in the process of maintaining its Throughput or Wealth.
concepts.name: Consumption

concepts.description: A Tax collected on specific Goods purchased by Pop to meet their Pop Needs. Each Good subject to Consumption Taxes costs a certain amount of Authority. When applied to a Good, its Market Price increases by the Consumption Tax rate at point of sale to Pops only, with all Buy Orders generated in this manner resulting in the surcharge being collected by the Treasury. Since the surcharge is applied on the Market level, the Tax is ineffective in States with low Market Access.
concepts.name: Consumption Tax

concepts.description: A Tax collected on the Consumption of Goods. Goods subject to Consumption Taxes will have its Market Price increased by the Consumption Tax Rate, and whenever Pops buy it this increase will be collected by the Treasury. Buildings are exempt from paying Consumption Taxes.
concepts.name: Consumption Taxes

concepts.description:
Articles in Treaties that have Non-Fulfillment conditions can be Contravened. For an Article to be considered Contravened, the responsible Country must have failed to meet the requirements of that Article. Whether the responsible Country is Contravening to an Article is checked weekly, monthly, yearly, or any combination thereof, depending on the Article.

For example, in the … Article, if the specified Law has not been Enacted or is not actively Enacting for 3 consecutive weeks, the Article is considered to be Non-Fulfilled until the Law is being Enacted again.

The number of consecutive Contraventions before Non-Fulfillment may differ between Articles.
concepts.name: Contravention

concepts.description:
Control represents the Makhzen's authority over the remote tribes of Morocco.

There is a bar for each surrounding State to the Capital State. A higher value indicates that the tribesfolk respect and fear the Government's decisions more, thus enabling officials to carry out their tasks effectively. Each state's starting negative Modifier scales monthly based on its current value. Greater Control results in less effective penalties, and vice versa.

By developing the chaotic state centers, creating more job opportunities, and fostering connections between urban and rural life, the tribes will gradually be influenced, reducing their isolation. Ultimately, their influence over the tribesmen will fade away.

Failing to maintain Control can prepare our downfall, leaving behind long-lasting effects on these states.
concepts.name: Control over the Lands of Anarchy

concepts.description: If the holder of a War Goal, or their Allies, Occupy at least … of the required State or States, they are considered to have Control of this War Goal. War Support can only drop below 0 if the opposing side Controls all their War Goals.
concepts.name: Controlled War Goal

concepts.description: Pops whose Religion has low Acceptance in the Country they live in may instead Convert to one with higher Acceptance. Pops that contain Radicals will convert at a reduced rate, and conversion is much slower in Unincorporated States.
concepts.name: Conversion

concepts.description: This Ideology is what the Supporting Pops and Agitators care about and what the Political Movement as a whole will be pushing for. Passing Laws Endorsed by this Ideology will create Loyalists from Supporting Pops. If any Interest Groups are Pressured, this is guranteed to be one of the Character Ideologies to become possible for new Leaders of those Interest Groups.
concepts.name: Core Movement Ideology

concepts.description:
The Countdown to War phase is the third and last phase of a Diplomatic Play. War might now be inevitable, with both sides frantically making preparations or considering any last-minute options to back down.

Typical preparations for War includes: Mobilization of Armies, giving their Generals Orders to advance or defend the Fronts, Drafting Conscript Battalions, and promoting your Generals to increase their Command Limit where necessary.
concepts.name: Countdown to War

concepts.description:
A Country consists of one or several parcels of Land organized into States, in which a Population resides under the rule of a Government and its Head of State. In Victoria 3, both human and AI players each control a Country.

Aside from the nature of their Pops, which States they own, and how they been developed, a Country is defined also by their Country Tier, Primary Cultures, and State Religion, and whether they are Recognized or Unrecognized. Countries also have different Laws and access to different Technologies.
concepts.name: Country

concepts.description: A Country Monopoly gives a Country a Monopoly on a Building with exclusive Building rights of that Industry. The Goods produced by a Monopoly will increase in price up to 20% proportionate to this … Sell Orders share at the World Market.
concepts.name: Country Monopoly

concepts.description: A Country’s Tier is the inherent status and Prestige it is granted based on its history and significance. Forming a new Country is only possible if its Tier is higher than the Country's current one.
concepts.name: Country Tier

concepts.description:
The act of unifying and forming a new Country out of several Countries is called Unification. A Country can be formed by controlling a specific number of States in the new Country's region.

A Major Unification allows Countries to become Unification Candidates which gives them access to the Unification Diplomatic Play. This Diplomatic Play sets the War Goals to annex all the required States and Countries.

While a Minor Unification do not allow any Unification Candidates and can only form a Country if the number of required States are controlled.
concepts.name: Country Unification

concepts.description:
A Coup is an attempt by a Commander with low Loyalty to overthrow the sitting Government. The risk of a Coup increases when a Country is ruled by a Government with low Legitimacy, or if a disloyal Commander has a high concept_commander_rank_short and Popularity.

Once a Coup begins, if its progress reaches 100%, the commander executing the Coup will issue a Pronunciamento. A successful Pronunciamento will cause the overthrow of the Government.

The progress of a Coup is determined by the Coup Strength of the commander executing the Coup, evaluated against the Coup Resistance of the sitting government.
concepts.name: Coup

concepts.description:
Coup Resistance represents the ability for a Government to fend off a Coup by a Commander. A Coup will retreat when the Coup Resistance of the sitting Government is higher than the Coup Strength of the Commander orchestrating the Coup.

Factors contributing to Coup Resistance include:
• High Government Legitimacy
• Level of … investment under … or … Laws
concepts.name: Coup Resistance

concepts.description:
Coup Strength represents the ability for a Commander to successfully orchestrate a Coup against the sitting Government. A Coup will progress when the Commander's Interest Group's Approval is negative, and the Coup Strength of the Commander orchestrating the Coup is higher than the Coup Resistance of the sitting government.

Factors contributing to Coup Strength include:
• High Popularity
• High Commander Rank
• Clout of Commander Interest Group
• Proximity of the Commander's Formation to the Capital State
concepts.name: Coup Strength

concepts.description:
Court Intrigue represents the progress of various plots to overthrow the Maharaja (Ruler). Intrigue is tracked in the Sikh Sovereignty Journal Entry. If Intrigue reaches 100%, the Maharaja (Ruler) will be assassinated, Empire Stability will be reset to 0, Intrigue will decrease, and a new candidate will be enthroned.

The following conditions decrease Court Intrigue: 
• Maharaja (Ruler) is Ranjit Singh
• … Leaders In Government with Approval above 5
• … Leaders In Government
• Ruler Interest Group is Powerful
• High Legitimacy
• Events and other effects 

The following conditions increase Court Intrigue: 
• … Ruler
• Low Ruler Popularity
• … Leaders In Government or In Opposition with Approval below 0
• … Leaders In Government or In Opposition with Approval below 0
• Ruler Interest Group is Marginalized
• Low Legitimacy
• Events and other effects
concepts.name: Court Intrigue

concepts.description: The national Credit is the amount of Money the Treasury can borrow from its economy, equal to the sum of all domestic Cash Reserves plus a base value determined by Gross Domestic Product. If the Principal exceeds the Credit Limit the Country goes into Default.
concepts.name: Credit

concepts.description: An increase or decrease to the amount of damage a Ship can deal to another Ship’s crew
concepts.name: Crew Attack Damage

concepts.description: How many Casualties a Fleet has taken in battle.
concepts.name: Crew Casualties

concepts.description:
An increase or decrease to the probability that the Ship will get a critical hit when attacking. 
Critical hits ignore … of the targets Ship Armor.
concepts.name: Critical Chance

concepts.description: A bonus or penalty to the amount of damage dealt when a Ship gets a critical hit when attacking
concepts.name: Critical Damage

concepts.description: A Crown Land is a Subject Type that cannot start their own Diplomatic Plays yet are forced to join their Overlord’s Wars, and must also pay 40% of their Treasury income to their Overlord each week. A Crown Land's Rank cannot increase to match or exceed their Overlord's, and their Overlord may target them with the Annexation Diplomatic Play.
concepts.name: Crown Land

concepts.description: A Crown Land is an administrative region of a dynastic empire, retaining varying levels of regional autonomy.
concepts.name: Crown Land

concepts.description:
A Cultural Community indicates a certain Culture is present in a State and allows Pops in your Market to migrate to this State.

A newly formed Community will have lower Acceptance, but this will go away over time. A new Law that changes Acceptance may also take time to implement, so Pops of that Community will temporarily have a different Acceptance from the norm.
concepts.name: Cultural Community

concepts.description:
Cultural Movements are Political Movements pursuing a better life for people of a specific Culture. If this culture is the Primary Culture of a Country, the movement will push a nationalistic agenda. Otherwise, the movement will push for Laws which give their people greater Acceptance, or even attempt a Secession.

If a Cultural Movement's Movement Activism exceeds Protesting (…), it will begin to generate Obstinance in States with Supporting Pops.
concepts.name: Cultural Movement

concepts.description: The Turmoil generated by Pops of a specific Culture, generally from its proportion of Radicals. If its value in a Country is at least …, it might trigger a Mass Migration of that Culture to another Country. Alternatively, at high enough values, those Pops may instead attempt to separate their Homelands in a Secession.
concepts.name: Cultural Turmoil

concepts.description: All Pops have a Culture, which can only change through Assimilation. Their Culture determines which State Regions they consider their Homelands and affects their Acceptance Status in their Country.
concepts.name: Culture

concepts.description: An enforced pact between a Senior Partner and one or several Junior Partners to share a single Market, under the leadership of the Senior Partner. Usually enforced via a Power Bloc Principle. Additionally, all Subject Pacts also act as a Customs Union.
concepts.name: Customs Union

concepts.description: Casualties that end up Dead due to Battle or Attrition.
concepts.name: Dead

concepts.description: A Decaying effect will gradually decrease in intensity, starting from its initial value and decreasing linearly down to 0 over the stated decay duration.
concepts.name: Decay

concepts.description:
A Nation that share most properties of Countries - Pops, a Ruler, Buildings, Laws and so on - but with a lack of centralized power (and/or will) to enforce borders. This makes them prone to Colonization by Countries who do not see them as equals to be properly Negotiated with for land rights.

Decentralized Nations are AI controlled and are not playable by humans.
concepts.name: Decentralized Nation

concepts.description:
Large projects that can be undertaken by a nation will appear as Decisions, including expeditions across the globe and the construction of man-made canals. 

Decisions can be found underneath Journal Entries in the Journal.
concepts.name: Decision

concepts.description: Decrees are demands made by a Country’s Ruler to effect changes in a State under their control. Decrees cost Authority for as long as they are active. Once issued, the Decree will provide a certain bonus to the State until it is removed.
concepts.name: Decree

concepts.description: Once the Treasury accumulates Loans large enough that they exceed the Country’s total Credit, the Country is considered to be in Default. This will pause all ongoing Construction and will have a negative impact on the Throughput of Buildings, growing more severe as time passes. Penalties are removed as soon as the Country's weekly balance becomes positive again, or if Bankruptcy is declared.
concepts.name: Default

concepts.description: These are … Military Units in Armies.
concepts.name: Default Unit

concepts.description: An Admiral is Defeated when he loses a Battle at sea. A Fleet is Defeated when all its Admirals are Defeated. Admirals and Fleets will only repair and regroup once they are back at their home HQ and their Ships have regained at least … of their total Manpower.
concepts.name: Defeated

concepts.description: A Military Unit’s fighting ability in Battle while defending from enemy incursions.
concepts.name: Defense

concepts.description: A Treaty Article that is a limited Alliance between two Countries, which only comes into effect in Diplomatic Plays where one of the two is the Target of the Play.
concepts.name: Defensive Pact

concepts.description:
A Military Unit’s Morale measures how much of its remaining Manpower is ready for Battle. In each round of combat, some of the remaining Manpower will become Demoralized for the remainder of the Battle and unable to take offensive action. As all Military Units reach a critical threshold of low Morale the Commander will retreat, leaving the other side victorious.

After a Battle, Military Units will regain their Morale at a steady rate depending on the Supply of their Formation.
concepts.name: Demoralized

concepts.description: At the end of each week, Pops receive a Dependent Income based on their number of Dependents and the amount of income they qualify for. Most Dependents receive a base amount from odd jobs depending on the Pop's Profession, which can be supplemented by the … Institution.
concepts.name: Dependent Income

concepts.description:
The part of a Pop not considered part of the Workforce. They represent the families of the Working Adults and normally constitute the majority of the population. Dependents usually generate Dependent Income that is typically smaller than the Wages collected by Working Adults, but they also have lower Pop Needs. While they are able to support Interest Groups their Political Strength typically count for less. They are only granted Voting Rights under very specific Laws.

Enacting different Laws or maintaining certain Institutions may convert Dependents into Working Adults over time, increase their Political Strength, or supplement their Dependent Income.
concepts.name: Dependents

concepts.description:
An increase or decrease to how easily the Ship will detect other Ships

A Fleet’s Detection and the enemies Visibility are used in conjunction to determine the chance to spawn a Naval Battle and how many Ships will be involved.
concepts.name: Detection

concepts.description:
Devastation is the damage done to a State Region as a result of war or natural disasters. It increases from Battles and when under hostile Occupation. It will decrease over time if no part of the State Region is at war.

Devastation has a negative impact on Infrastructure, Mortality, Throughput, and Migration Attraction.
concepts.name: Devastation

concepts.description: A broad term for interactions between two Countries that includes Instant Diplomatic Actions, Ongoing Diplomatic Actions, and Diplomatic Pacts. They differ from Diplomatic Plays in that no third party is allowed to have a say in its outcome, and there is no risk the action on its own might escalate into War.
concepts.name: Diplomatic Action

concepts.description:
A Diplomatic Catalyst is essentially any diplomatic occurence, which may create Political Lobbies or change a Country’s Attitude towards you.

Catalysts can be any change on the world stage, for example:
• Diplomatic Actions
• Actions taken in Diplomatic Plays
• Change in Relations levels
concepts.name: Diplomatic Catalyst

concepts.description: A Diplomatic Demand is a single War Goal which one Country demands from another. If the Diplomatic Demand is rejected, a Diplomatic Play will start with the demanded War Goal as the Primary Demand of the Initiator.
concepts.name: Diplomatic Demand

concepts.description: A Diplomatic Incident is typically the result of a Country starting a Diplomatic Play. Diplomatic Incidents generate Infamy for the Country who started it, and will cause Relations to fall with all Countries with an Interest in the Strategic Region, particularly the target of the Play. Diplomatic Incidents can also be the result of other actions, for example decisions made during special events.
concepts.name: Diplomatic Incident

concepts.description: View the Attitude of other Countries and monitor your Interests and their Strategic Regions, establish Diplomatic Pacts and take Actions, and start Diplomatic Plays.
concepts.name: Diplomatic Lens

concepts.description: The Diplomatic Maneuvers phase is the second phase of a Diplomatic Play. In this phase, the Initiator and Target can attempt to Sway other Countries to their side or claim additional War Goals for themselves, at the cost of Maneuvers.
concepts.name: Diplomatic Maneuvers

concepts.description: Unilateral or bilateral understandings between two Countries. They may have a maintenance cost in Influence for one or both parties, and can have a wide range of effects including Subject relationships. Pacts can break for a number of different reasons, including Relations deviating too far in either direction, one side or another explicitly breaking it, or a time limit running out.
concepts.name: Diplomatic Pact

concepts.description: Money collected from or remitted to the other Country in a Diplomatic Pact.
concepts.name: Diplomatic Pacts

concepts.description:
A Diplomatic Play is a period of hostile diplomatic negotiations between two or more Countries that follows after one Country makes a demand for a concession by another. To start a Diplomatic Play you must have a high enough Interest Tier in the relevant Strategic Region, which also entitles you to participate in Plays as a third party in that Strategic Region.

The Diplomatic Play will Escalate through three phases: Opening Moves, Diplomatic Maneuvers, and Countdown to War. These phases set the terms for a possible Peace Deal should the Diplomatic Play Escalate into a War. A War can be averted if either the Initiator or Target of the Play backs down and grants the other their Primary Demands.
concepts.name: Diplomatic Play

concepts.description:
Having Diplomatic Relevancy is required for a Country to engage in certain interactions like signing Treaties. A Country is considered Diplomatically Relevant for another if one of the following conditions is fulfilled:
• They share a direct border
• They share a direct border with only one Sea Node between them
• One Country is bordering a Subject of the other
• One Country’s Subject is bordering the other Country’s Subject
• An existing Treaty between the two Countries
• Both Countries being Great Powers
• One of the Countries declaring a Rivalry towards the other
• One of the Countries conducting Piracy targetting the other
• Both Countries having overlapping Interests
concepts.name: Diplomatic Relevancy

concepts.description:
Pops can be Discriminated Against if their Culture and/or Religion have a low Acceptance value in their Country. Typically, Pops in the lower three Acceptance statuses are considered to be Discriminated. Discriminated Pops:
- get paid less than their peers
- have less Political Strength
- are less likely to develop Qualifications for certain Profession
- naturally become Radical over time
- and are more likely to Emigrate.

In addition, certain Laws limit or expand national acceptance of Culture and Religions.
concepts.name: Discrimination

concepts.description:
Aspects of a Culture or Religion that determine how Accepted Pops of that Culture or Religion are depending on how similar they are to the Country's Primary Culture and State Religion and what … Law the Country currently has.

For a Culture, these aspects are its Heritage, Language and any Traditions it might have. A Religion only has a Heritage Trait.

Heritage and Language Traits also belong to broader Groups of similar Traits.
concepts.name: Discrimination Trait

concepts.description: A Discrimination Trait Group is a broader collection of Discrimination Traits that share a common origin somehow, making them more recognizable to and accepted by Pops of the same Trait Group.
concepts.name: Discrimination Trait Group

concepts.description: A Disenfranchised Pop is prohibited from participating in the Country’s politics. As a result they cannot support any Interest Groups. The most common reason for a Pop to be Disenfranchised is low Acceptance.
concepts.name: Disenfranchised

concepts.description: A Culture is Disqualified for the purposes of organizing the United States of Greater Austria if its demands are refused. Typically, this occurs as a result of Integrating a different Culture with which the culture to be Disqualified shares Homeland States. Disqualified Cultures may not be negotiated with further, or Integrated under any circumstances.
concepts.name: Disqualified Culture

concepts.description:
While Privately Owned Buildings have a positive Balance, some of this profit is paid out to the owning Pops as Dividends, which are subject to Dividends Taxes.

Depending on the Country’s current …, a portion of Pop Dividends may be invested back into the economy through Reinvestment, while the remainder goes towards Pop Needs and Wealth.

If a Building is fully or partially Nationally Owned, profits can be payed out as Government Dividends instead.
concepts.name: Dividends

concepts.description: A Tax applied to the Dividends earned by Pops with Privately Owned Buildings.
concepts.name: Dividends Taxes

concepts.description: Recognized Powers may turn a weaker Country into their Dominion (Subject). A Dominion is a more autonomous Subject Type that are able to start their own Diplomatic Plays and are forced to join their Overlord’s Wars. They must pay 25% of their Treasury income to their Overlord each week.
concepts.name: Dominion

concepts.description:
Dynastic Loyalty represents the Serbian population's support for keeping the ruling dynasty on the throne, as opposed to their rivals. The ruling dynasty must gain enough support to prevent the opposition from voicing a claim. Failing to do so will cause them to lose the throne, and stagnate national growth.

The following conditions will advance Dynastic Loyalty:
• High Ruler Popularity
• Low Popularity of rival claimants
• High Legitimacy 
• High Standard of Living
• Fraction of Loyalists
• Non-Marginalized Interest Groups In Opposition above 4 Approval by Clout 
• Has … or … enacted
• Not being a Subject
• Each Major Power or Great Power supporting our independence
• Events or other choices

The following conditions will deplete Dynastic Loyalty:
• Low Ruler Popularity
• High Popularity of rival claimants
• Low Legitimacy
• Low Standard of Living
• Fraction of Radicals
• Non-Marginalized Interest Groups In Opposition below -4 Approval by Clout 
• Negative Authority
• Negative Bureaucracy
• Positive Relations with Overlord
• Events or other choices
concepts.name: Dynastic Loyalty

concepts.description:
Economic Dependence is the amount of economic reliance two Countries have between one another. The main influence of which is the amount of Buildings that are owned by the other Country. This can either be through direct ownership from a Country or by Pop investors.

Being in a shared market will additionally take into consideration the difference in Gross Domestic Product and the impact of each Countries’ produced Goods and owned Buildings on Pops.

If the two Countries are not in a shared market, the Economic Dependence is impacted by Trade. The impact of this is dependent on the amount of Trade between the two Countries and the impact on Good Market Balance.
concepts.name: Economic Dependence

concepts.description:
A Country’s economy is considered Healthy if either:
• its fixed incomes exceed its fixed expenses
• its Principal is less than half their total Credit
concepts.name: Economy Health

concepts.description:
Many Buildings become more efficient the larger they get. Such Buildings gain the following effects for every Building Level beyond the first:
……
concepts.name: Economy of Scale

concepts.description: The degree by which a Pop is able to access education for their children. As new generations are born and raised, the Pop's Literacy will move towards its level of Education Access.
concepts.name: Education Access

concepts.description:
Countries with a Voting Franchise will hold Elections every … years. An Election campaign period will commence … months prior to the date, during which Parties will vie for Momentum and Votes.

On Election day the final Votes will be tallied, which will affect the Political Strength of the member Interest Groups of each Party. Under certain Government Types a new Head of State may also be selected as a result of the Election's outcome. Finally, a single Government Reform may be performed where any Interest Groups may be removed from Government without generating any new Radicals.
concepts.name: Election

concepts.description: Electoral Confidence is a measure in how much the electorate of a Country trusts that any elections held will be free and fair. Tampering with elections by rigging them in favor of a specific Party will lower Electoral Confidence, while allowing elections to proceed without interference will increase it. A low Electoral Confidence will impact Legitimacy and the amount of Political Strength gained from votes, with the degree of effect varying based on your enacted Laws and Amendments.
concepts.name: Electoral Confidence

concepts.description: An Ongoing Diplomatic Action established by one Country targeting another, which reduces the Trade Advantage of the target Country for exporting Goods to the country enforcing the embargo via the World Market. Countries that are at War will automatically Embargo each other.
concepts.name: Embargo

concepts.description: The Emperor, or Tennō, is the traditional ruler of Japan, as well as the head of the Shinto Religion. Throughout the Tokugawa period, the Emperor has remained secluded within the Imperial Palace in Kyōto, with their affairs tightly regulated by the Shogunate.
concepts.name: Emperor

concepts.description:
Empire Stability represents the strength of the Maharaja (Ruler). Stability is tracked in the Sikh Sovereignty Journal Entry.

Legitimacy must be above 50 for Stability to increase. If Court Intrigue reaches 100%, the Maharaja (Ruler) will be assassinated, Stability will be reset to 0, Intrigue will decrease, and a new candidate will be enthroned.

The following conditions increase Empire Stability: 
• … Interest Group is In Government
• … Interest Group is Powerful
• … is the State Religion
• … Law is Enacted
• Events and other conditions 

The following conditions decrease Empire Stability: 
• … Interest Group is not In Government
• Court Intrigue reaches 100%
• Events and other conditions
concepts.name: Empire Stability

concepts.description: A Pop working in a Building is said to be Employed. Employment provides the Pop with a Wage. An Employed Pop can switch jobs if a job with a better Wage appears as long as they have the Qualifications for it.
concepts.name: Employment

concepts.description: Enactment Advance indicates the percentage chance that the enactment process of a Law will advance somehow at the next checkpoint, even if it won't complete or progress to the next Phase yet. It is derived from the enactment's Base Success chance.
concepts.name: Enactment Advance

concepts.description: Enactment Debate indicates the percentage chance that the enactment process of a Law will meet with some kind of complication at the next checkpoint. The lower the total chances of Success, Advance, and Stall the greater the chance of Debate.
concepts.name: Enactment Debate

concepts.description:
The act of attempting to push a new Law through several Phases in the Country’s legislature. At regular intervals the Law's Enactment Success chance will be tested. The time between tests can vary by law, and is also dependent on the Government’s Legitimacy. If the Law does not progress to the next Enactment Phase, it will either Advance, be Debated, or Stall which affects its chances to pass the next test or introduce other consequences to your Country.n
For a Law to be able to be Enacted it must be Endorsed by at least one Interest Group In Government, supported by a current Political Movement, or have a positive Enactment Success chance for some other reason.
concepts.name: Enactment of Laws

concepts.description: To Enact a Law you must successfully guide it through … Phases …by achieving Successes. During this process there is a risk of getting Enactment Setbacks that may cause the Enactment to fail.
concepts.name: Enactment Phase

concepts.description:
While Enacting a Law you may suffer Setbacks. This could be due to a Stall result at the Enactment checkpoint, a consequence of a Debate, or that Enactment Success chance fell below 0. If you accumulate too many Setbacks, the Enactment fails.

If the enactment fails, you will not be able to attempt to enact that Law again for … days.
concepts.name: Enactment Setback

concepts.description: Enactment Success indicates the percentage chance that a Law will progress to the next Phase at the next checkpoint. It is equal to the Base Success chance plus any effects accumulated during the enactment process. The Base Success chance is increased by support from an Interest Group In Government, a Political Movement with at least Agitating 25% Movement Activism, or Endorsement from the Ruler’s Ideology.
concepts.name: Enactment Success

concepts.description: The presence of a End-of-Discussion Factor represents that Interest Groups in Government consider further discussion of the merits of the Law currently being enacted no longer useful. The lower this factor gets, the more negative pressure it puts on the possibility that the enactment may Advance or Stall.
concepts.name: End-of-Discussion Factor

concepts.description: An Interest Group’s Endorsement or Opposition of a Law is determined by their Ideologies. For a Law to be able to be Enacted it must be Endorsed by at least one Interest Group In Government, supported by a current Political Movement, or have a positive Enactment Success chance for some other reason.
concepts.name: Endorsement and Opposition to Laws

concepts.description:
An Enforced Treaty is a Treaty forced upon a Country from backing down in a Diplomatic Play or capitulating in a War. Some Diplomatic Demands can also turn into an Enforced Treaty.

It is made up of War Reparations or Diplomatic Demands containing individual Articles that define the rights, duties and Influence cost for the capitulating Country. Enforced Treaties remain in effect until the demanding side breaks the agreement or either side withdraws from it after the initial Binding Period has passed.
concepts.name: Enforced Treaty

concepts.description: Once a Diplomatic Play has been initiated, it steadily Escalates through three distinct phases: Opening Moves, Diplomatic Maneuvers, and Countdown to War. The phase limits which actions are available to participants. If the Play does not resolve prior to Escalation progressing all the way through the Countdown to War, War will break out.
concepts.name: Escalation

concepts.description: Executives are the Characters that lead a Company. Like other Characters they can have Character Traits which influence how good they are at their job. They provide Clout to their Interest Group based on how well their Company is doing. Executives can also become Leader of an Interest Group.
concepts.name: Executive

concepts.description: Executives are the Characters that lead a Company. Like other Characters they can have Character Traits which influence how good they are at their job. They provide Clout to their Interest Group based on how well their Company is doing. Executives can also become Leader of an Interest Group.
concepts.name: Executives

concepts.description:
A Character may be Exiled using the Exile Dissident character action. The Character becomes an Agitator and is expelled from your country.

An Exiled Character may be invited to any Country through the Invite Exile character action, where they will immediately start or join a Political Movement for that Country in accordance with their Ideology. If all their Endorsed Laws are already active when they arrive, the invited Agitator will remain dormant.

An Exiled Character can only be invited if their Acceptance Status is one of the following in your Country: … or ….
concepts.name: Exile

concepts.description: Armies can become Exiled when their Front cannot be reached any longer and they cannot find a valid alternative. This can happen for example when they are fully surrounded. An Exiled Army will move to the nearest HQ before it can be sent to another Front or be given other Orders again. While doing so, the Army will suffer from Attrition.
concepts.name: Exiled Army

concepts.description:
Experience determines the Veterancy Rank of Military Units and of the Crew in Ships. Once they have enough Experience, they are promoted to a higher Rank.

 For Military Units, Experience is gained over time, more when mobilized and during battles.

For Ships, not being on a Naval Mission will cause its Crew to lose Experience over time.
concepts.name: Experience

concepts.description: The price at which a Good is exported to the World Market in a specific State. This is based on both the World Market Price and the State’s relative Trade Advantage.
concepts.name: Export Price

concepts.description:
A Famine is the result of a large part of the Population in a State suffering from Starvation. It is primarily a political classification meant to bring attention to the plight of the ones in need in your society.

A Famine is declared in a State if all of these conditions are fulfilled:
• at least … of the Population is Starving
• at least … is suffering from Severe Starvation.
• the state does not belong to a Decentralized Nation
concepts.name: Famine

concepts.description: Notifications that appear in chronological order in the feed in the bottom-right corner of the screen.
concepts.name: Feed

concepts.description:
Fervor is a measure of the national spirit of a Culture. Pops of a Culture with high Fervor will Assimilate more slowly, form more Radicals when conquered, increase Liberty Desire and be more likely to join Cultural Movements.

The following conditions increase Fervor: 
• Being a Primary Culture of an independent Country with an #tooltippable;tooltip:…,fervor_effects_from_citizenship_laws_tt applicable … Law
• Number of Casualties of this Culture in War
• Having high average Literacy
• Number of … Pops of this Culture
• Pops of this culture resident in Countries with … or … Technologies
• Being a Primary Culture of a Country with an applicable … Institution
• Other Culture released as independent Countries
• Experiencing a National Awakening

The following conditions decrease Fervor: 
• Being a Primary Culture of a Country with the … Law
• Having high average Acceptance
concepts.name: Fervor

concepts.description: A Flagship is the lead Ship of the Country's Navy. Only one Flagship can exist at a time. Winning battles involving the Flagship will provide additional Prestige to the Country that owns it, whereas losing them will harm the Prestige.
concepts.name: Flagship

concepts.description:
A Fleet is a naval Formation composed of Ships, led by an Admiral who lends bonuses from his Character Traits and Orders to the whole Formation.

It can be sent on Naval Missions like …, …, and … covering several Sea Regions, clashing in Naval Battles with any enemy Fleets that they find (or that find them).

Fleets tend to take a long time to build up, and many Ships become obsolete over time as they cannot always be upgraded. Think carefully before investing too heavily into large Fleets.
concepts.name: Fleet

concepts.description: The average Hit Points of all Ships in a Fleet represent the Fleet’s average durability and ability to withstand damage in naval combat.
concepts.name: Fleet Hit Points

concepts.description:
Food Security measures how easy or difficult it is for a Pop to acquire all the food it requires to survive. If a Pop's Food Security gets too low, it will start suffering from Starvation. The lower Food Security goes, the harsher the effects of Starvation will be.

There are two main factors that affect Food Security. The first of them is the Shortage level for the … Need. The second factor is based on how much Money the Pop is spending on … compared to the Pop's expected expenses at base cost.
concepts.name: Food Security

concepts.description:
A Country constructing and owning Building Levels in another Country.

Foreign Investments can be made by an Overlord in its Subjects, or between two sovereign Countries by signing a Foreign Investment Rights Treaty.

Both Government Construction and Private Construction are allowed via Foreign Investment.

While the foreign owner constructs the Building Levels and gains Dividends, the Workforce comes from the local State, and Taxes are paid to the Country controlling that State. Any Goods used by the Building remains in the local Market.
concepts.name: Foreign Investment

concepts.description: Permits one Country to do Foreign Investment in another for the duration of the Treaty. Additionally the Treaty allows Companies to construct a Regional Company HQ if they are given the Investment Rights Company Charter.
concepts.name: Foreign Investment Rights

concepts.description: A Formation is an Army or Fleet that is used in Wars to achieve military objectives. They may have assigned Military Units and a Commander and can be ordered to Fronts to fight the enemy forces there.
concepts.name: Formation

concepts.description: A collection of Provinces on the border of Theaters between two Countries at War with each other. Generals can be Ordered to advance or defend Fronts, which can result in Battles that change the size of the Theaters and the location of the Front.
concepts.name: Front

concepts.description: A Country’s fully mobilized Battalions include all Battalions in Mobilized Armies that have already undergone Mobilization and are fully prepared to follow any of their Army's Generals into Battle.
concepts.name: Fully Mobilized Battalions

concepts.description: One Country pays part of its income to the Pops of another, based on the weekly tax revenue of the recipient. This action has a chance each week to create or strengthen friendly Lobbies in the target Country.
concepts.name: Fund Lobbies

concepts.description: A Country’s Gross Domestic Product can be both domestically owned by the Country itself and foreignly owned by other Countries. If another Country has Investment Rights, they may foreignly own Building Levels in the initial Country. The GDP generated from those Building Levels then contribute to the foreign Country’s GDP. Only domestically owned GDP contributes to the domestic Country’s Prestige and Minting.
concepts.name: GDP Ownership

concepts.description: An Army’s Commander is called a General who leads the Army's Battalions into Battle. You can change any General's Order on the Army Formation panel or by right-clicking the General at any time. What Orders you may give a General depends on his Character Traits, but there will always be the basic Advance and Defend Orders. Any other military effects from a General's Character Traits may affect his Army as a whole or are applied onto Battalions under his direct command when in a Battle.
concepts.name: General

concepts.description:
Generated Pollution is how much total pollution the buildings in a State Region produce. How much Pollution Impact a State Region has is also dependent on the amount of Arable Land in that State Region.

A State Region with a lot of Arable Land will see Generated Pollution increase Pollution Impact by a smaller amount than a State Region with little Arable Land.
concepts.name: Generated Pollution

concepts.description: A Geographic Region is an area that corresponds to a collection of Strategic Regions and State Regions. Geographic Regions are unchanging but may overlap and in some cases can be a part of a larger Geographic Region altogether.
concepts.name: Geographic Region

concepts.description: A Country’s weekly budget surplus is accumulated in its Gold Reserves. If the budget balance becomes negative, any Money in the Gold Reserves will be depleted first before the Country starts taking Loans. The Gold Reserves can only accumulate up to a fraction of your Gross Domestic Product before diminishing returns set in. Stockpiling gold will eventually lead to depleting your economic engine.
concepts.name: Gold Reserves

concepts.description: A Buddha manifesting as a kami, pairing an indigenous deity with a bringer of Buddhist enlightenment.
concepts.name: Gongen

concepts.description: Goods are Produced in Buildings and are Consumed by Buildings and Pops. Goods have both a Local Price and a Market Price.
concepts.name: Good

concepts.description: Goods Consumed by a Country’s Government Buildings.
concepts.name: Goods for Government Buildings

concepts.description: Goods Consumed by Military Buildings and Ship upkeep.
concepts.name: Goods for Military Upkeep

concepts.description: An adjustment to the amount of Goods Consumed by a Building.
concepts.name: Goods Input

concepts.description:
A Pop Need can be fulfilled by any of the Goods it consists of, and the availability of each Good determines how much it is consumed.

For example, the … Pop Need contains both … and …. Pops will typically consume more … and less …. However, if … becomes more available than …, they will shift towards consuming more … and less … instead. In some cases, Pops may even stop consuming a Good entirely if there is no availability for that Good.

Additionally, Cultural Obsessions and Religious Taboos can significantly affect the consumption of certain Goods.

Goods with a higher Base Price will contribute more to fulfilling a Pop Need than those with a lower Base Price. For instance, a single unit of … is equivalent to several units of ….
concepts.name: Goods Substitution

concepts.description:
A Country’s Government consists of one or several Interest Groups. If the Country has Voting Rights these Interest Groups may be organized into Parties. Depending on the Country's Laws, this mix of Interest Groups will result in higher or lower Government Legitimacy.

Any new Law you wish to Enact must have some support among Interest Groups that make up the Government, unless it is supported by an active Political Movement. The ability to quickly and painlessly push the Law through the legislature depends on how unified the Government's support of it is.
concepts.name: Government

concepts.description:
A Building owned and operated by the Government using funds from the Treasury.

Government Buildings have no Goods Production and therefore no Revenue, but produce a number of other resources crucial to running a Country such as Bureaucracy, Infrastructure, …, and Military Units.

The Workforce of non-military Government Buildings get paid according to the Government Wage, while Military Buildings get paid according to the Military Wage.

Government Buildings are always fully Nationally Owned
concepts.name: Government Building

concepts.description:
A Government Construction is a Building that is being expanded on the direct orders of a Country’s Government.

It can draw funds directly from the state treasury and can be reprioritized or removed from the Construction Queue.

The resulting Building Levels become Nationally Owned
concepts.name: Government Construction

concepts.description:
While Nationally Owned Buildings have a positive Balance, some of these profits are paid directly to the Treasury as Government Dividends.

The amount paid depends on the proportion of Privately Owned to Nationally Owned Building Levels.
