In large economies with a high Gross Domestic Product, inefficiencies will also result in some of the profits being wasted. Additionally, Loans against Cash Reserves held by Nationally Owned Buildings will reduce the amount of Government Dividends that Buildings pay out.
concepts.name: Government Dividends

concepts.description: The total weekly Expenses accrued by the Government, balanced against all its weekly revenues such as Taxes, with the balance added to or removed from the Treasury.
concepts.name: Government Expenses

concepts.description: Goods Consumed by Government Buildings using funds from the Treasury.
concepts.name: Government Good

concepts.description: Coverage for services provided.
concepts.name: Government Premium

concepts.description: During a Government Reform you may alter the composition of your Government freely by granting or removing Interest Groups and/or Parties from power. Interest Groups removed from power during such a Reform will gain Radicals, unless the Reform is performed shortly after a concluded Election.
concepts.name: Government Reform

concepts.description: The upkeep of Slaves laboring directly for a Country’s government.
concepts.name: Government Slaves

concepts.description: A Country’s Government Type is determined by its Laws and determines its Transfer of Power, meaning who serves as its Head of State.…
concepts.name: Government Type

concepts.description: All Government Buildings except Military Buildings pay their Workforce according to the same standardized Government Wage rate. This rate is based on the Normal Wage in the Country, with any adjustments set in the Budget panel.
concepts.name: Government Wage

concepts.description: Wages paid to Pops by Government Buildings. The rate is based on the Country’s Normal Wage. You can adjust it up and down in the Budget panel.
concepts.name: Government Wages

concepts.description: Those few Countries that run the world through global empires or absolute local dominance are considered to be Great Power Rank. They are in a constant standoff with other Great Powers for an edge, and always wary of plucky Major Powers trying to ascend to greatness at their expense.…
concepts.name: Great Power

concepts.description:
Each unit of Goods … in your Country contributes to your Gross Domestic Product. The Market Price value of your national production is reduced by the value of Goods used as inputs into the process.

GDP affects Prestige and Minting.
concepts.name: Gross Domestic Product

concepts.description: Your country's Gross Domestic Product divided by its total Population.
concepts.name: Gross Domestic Product per Capita

concepts.description: A Treaty Article established by one Country targeting another, where the second Country is able to call the first to aid it in any Diplomatic Play where they are the defender.
concepts.name: Guarantee Independence

concepts.description:
A Guerilla War is a special kind of War subject to a set of rules distinct from regular warfare, the details of which can differ from one Guerilla War to another.

The following general rules are applied during a Guerilla War:
•  Battles are much smaller in size and created at a lower pace 
•  The …, … and … Battle Conditions can occur
•  Victories do not grant Occupation Score
•  A Guerilla War may escalate into a regular War if conflict specific conditions are met
concepts.name: Guerilla War

concepts.description:
A Harvest Condition is an occurrence that primarily affects a Country’s rural sector with a variable Intensity, duration, and range. It is generally a natural phenomenon and can have either positive or negative effects on the States it affects. Harvest Conditions will mostly affect the Throughput of agricultural Buildings, but they can also have an effect on your Population and States in other ways, such as reducing available Infrastructure.

Harvest Conditions will often affect States surrounding their epicenter. In such cases, the Harvest Condition Intensity will generally decrease as the distance to the epicenter increases.

Potential Harvest Conditions:
…
concepts.name: Harvest Condition

concepts.description: The Intensity of Harvest Condition multiplies its effects on a State. The closer a State is to the epicenter State Region, the higher the Intensity will most likely be.
concepts.name: Harvest Condition Intensity

concepts.description: A Country’s Ruler or highest representative. The Government Type determines who serves as the Head of State and when they are replaced.…
concepts.name: Head of State

concepts.description: A type of Poll Tax collected from all Pops whose Religion have low Acceptance ín their Country.
concepts.name: Heathen Taxes

concepts.description: The Heir of a Country is a Character. They will take over the Role of Ruler upon the current Ruler's death.
concepts.name: Heir

concepts.description: Heritage Traits represent the ancestry or foundation of a Culture or Religion. They also belong to a Trait Group, a broader family of similar Heritages.
concepts.name: Heritage Trait

concepts.description: A Holding is a Building (usually … or …) in the Home State of a Character, which the Character is presumed to own a considerable stake in. The type of Building that a Character will receive as their Holding is mainly dependent on their Interest Group.
concepts.name: Holding

concepts.description: A Character’s Home State is the State that they originate from. This is usually, but not always, a part of the Country the Character lives in. Magnates possess a Holding in their Home State, and gain Prominence based on its Revenue.
concepts.name: Home State

concepts.description:
A Culture’s Homelands consist of those State Regions that Pops of that Culture feel are historically or naturally their territory. Pops are more prone to Migrate to their Homelands than other States, and Pops who reside there will never consider Assimilating.

Launching a Diplomatic Play to conquer a State considered a Homeland of one of your Primary Cultures is considered relatively legitimate, and will generate substantially less Infamy than usual.
concepts.name: Homeland

concepts.description: The House of Karađorđević is one of the two contending Serb royal houses. They are descended from Karađorđe, leader of the ill-fated First Serbian Uprising against the Ottoman Empire. Supporters of the Karađorđević typically favor improved Relations with Russia.
concepts.name: House of Karađorđević

concepts.description: The House of Obrenović is one of the two contending Serb royal houses. They are descended from Miloš Obrenović, leader of the Second Serbian Uprising and founder of the autonomous Principality of Serbia. Supporters of the Obrenović typically favor improved Relations with Austria.
concepts.name: House of Obrenović

concepts.description: An HQ (Headquarter) is the territory owned by a Country in a particular Strategic Region. All Formations have a home HQ and can be stationed in HQs.
concepts.name: HQ

concepts.description: An increase or decrease to the amount of damage a Ship can deal to another Ship’s hull
concepts.name: Hull Attack Damage

concepts.description: A War Goal that can be claimed in a Diplomatic Play or as part of a Peace Deal. A Humiliated Country is unable to launch any Diplomatic Plays of their own against the Country they were Humiliated by for a duration of … months.…
concepts.name: Humiliation

concepts.description: A Government’s Legitimacy is reduced if the Interest Groups In Government have Ideologies that do not match the current Laws of the Country.
concepts.name: Ideological Incompatibility

concepts.description: An Interest Group’s Ideology influences which Laws it Endorses and Opposes. Their stance on the Laws which are currently in effect in the Country have small, permanent effects on the Interest Group's Approval. While a Country is trying to Enact a new Law, a larger but temporary effect applies relative to which Law is being removed and which is coming into effect. This temporary effect will eventually Decay, leaving only the permanent, objective effect on Approval.
concepts.name: Ideology

concepts.description: The price at which a Good is imported from the World Market in a specific State. This is based on both the World Market Price and the State’s relative Trade Advantage.
concepts.name: Import Price

concepts.description: Alerts that appear in the list when you click the Current Situations button.
concepts.name: Important Action

concepts.description: Interest Groups included in the Government affect which Laws can be Enacted and set the Country Legitimacy. They will never support Political Movements unless their Approval drops low enough that they leave to join the Opposition.
concepts.name: In Government

concepts.description: Interest Groups not part of the Government are considered In Opposition. Their only way to affect Enactment of Laws is through Political Movements, but their Interest Group Traits apply in full as usual.
concepts.name: In Opposition

concepts.description: A Tax collected on the Wages paid to the Workforce.
concepts.name: Income Taxes

concepts.description: States that are fully integrated into a Country. Pops in Incorporated States pay taxes, gain access to benefits from Institutions, and participate fully in the Country's political system. Unincorporated States can be Incorporated through a sometimes lengthy process.
concepts.name: Incorporated State

concepts.description: An individual is a single person within a Pop, who can be either a Working Adult or a Dependent. All Pops are made up of Individuals with the same Culture, Religion, Profession, and Workplace.
concepts.name: Individual

concepts.description: Infamy reflects the degree by which the international community, particularly the reigning Great Powers, see you as a threat to be contained in light of your past actions. It is accrued primarily from causing Diplomatic Incidents and claiming War Goals in a Peace Deal. Your Infamy affects Countries' Attitude towards you and increases the Influence cost of Diplomatic Pacts. If it reaches the level of Pariah, Great Powers will be able to start the … Diplomatic Play against you.
concepts.name: Infamy

concepts.description: Influence is a Capacity used for Diplomatic Actions, Pacts and Treaties targeting another Country. You gain based on your Rank.
concepts.name: Influence

concepts.description:
The amount of Clout an Interest Group has decides whether it is Powerful, Influential, or Marginalized. An Influential Interest Group's Interest Group Traits will have a lesser effect than if they were Powerful.

Interest Groups are considered Influential while their Clout is below ….
concepts.name: Influential

concepts.description: Infrastructure is provided by Buildings like … and …. It influences how well connected a State is to its Market, and how rapidly Battalions Mobilize.
concepts.name: Infrastructure

concepts.description: Buildings use a certain amount of Infrastructure depending on how technologically advanced or demanding they are. The total Infrastructure Usage in the State is compared to the Infrastructure to determine the State's Market Access. Infrastructure Usage also increases the cost of Port Connections.
concepts.name: Infrastructure Usage

concepts.description: The Country that initiated a Diplomatic Play.
concepts.name: Initiator

concepts.description: Innovation is produced by … Buildings and contributes to active research progress for Technologies. Unspent Innovation will increase the Technology Spread you're currently benefiting from, if any.
concepts.name: Innovation

concepts.description: Countries with such low Prestige they don't even qualify to be considered Minor Powers are of Insignificant Rank. They struggle for their right to self-determination while trying not to appear too inconvenient to nearby Major and Great Powers.…
concepts.name: Insignificant Power

concepts.description: An action with an instant effect on the Countries involved. They typically require a certain condition to be true in order to be taken but do not cost any Influence.
concepts.name: Instant Diplomatic Action

concepts.description: Institutions provide benefits to Incorporated States across your Country. They cost Bureaucracy to maintain in proportion to the number of Pops living in your Incorporated States and the Institution's investment level. Higher levels increase both the cost and the effect. Adjusting investment levels take a set amount of time.
concepts.name: Institution

concepts.description: An Insurrection is either a Secessionist or a Revolutionary Political Movement. This means the Movement is on the brink of turning into a Civil War. Any Pops or Interest Groups that are part of a Insurrectionary Movement are also labeled Insurrectionary.
concepts.name: Insurrection

concepts.description: An Integrated Culture is a Culture whose demands have been satisfactorily addressed during the process of organizing the United States of Greater Austria. When a Culture is Integrated, it becomes a Primary Culture, and contributes to the progress of the The Federal Solution Journal Entry. Integrated Cultures may become Disqualified if their demands are contradicted following their Integration. Disqualifying a Culture that has already been Integrated will lead to heavy penalties.
concepts.name: Integrated Culture

concepts.description: A Country maintaining an Interest in a Strategic Region signals to the rest of the world that they might get involved in Diplomatic Plays taking place there. Having a high enough Interest Tier in a Strategic Region is a requirement the ability to start or join Diplomatic Plays, and you cannot Colonize State Regions where you do not maintain a high enough Interest Tier.
concepts.name: Interest

concepts.description:
The Interest paid by a Country on its Loans. It is calculated by multiplying the Principal with the annual Interest Rate.

Interest is payed out to the Pops whose Privately Owned Cash Reserves are the basis for the Loans. Nationally Owned Buildings instead provide less Government Dividends.

The Interest Rate paid is affected primarily by Technology.
concepts.name: Interest

concepts.description:
A political faction within your Country that share a common interest. They are supported by Pops in relation to their Attraction to them, and the Clout they enjoy is based directly on the supporting Pops' Political Strength. Interest Groups have a number of Ideologies, causing them to Endorse or Oppose different Laws.

They also have three Interest Group Traits that are activated on different Approval levels. Their Leader’s personal Ideology also rubs off on the Interest Group.
concepts.name: Interest Group

concepts.description: How likely Pops are to support a particular Interest Group. Influenced by the Pop's properties, such as Profession, Wealth, and Education Access, a high Attraction means the Pop feels it's likely this Interest Group represents their political interests.
concepts.name: Interest Group Attraction

concepts.description:
All Interest Groups have three Traits that take effect on different levels of Approval and have a considerable impact on the whole Country.
A negative Trait will activate if Approval drops below Unhappy (…)
A positive Trait will activate if Approval exceeds Happy (…)
An additional positive Trait will activate if Approval exceeds Loyal (…).
Once active, the Trait will not deactivate until Approval is at least … points away from the threshold.

The Traits of Marginalized Interest Groups never activate, while the Traits of Powerful Interest Groups have increased effect.
concepts.name: Interest Group Trait

concepts.description:
An Interest Tier signifies the level of presence that a Country has in a Strategic Region and can be upgraded by increasing Involvement in a given Region.
Higher tiers unlock new interactions and benefits.
concepts.name: Interest Tier

concepts.description: An Army attacking a State via land or sea, the latter also being referred to as Naval Invasion.
concepts.name: Invasion

concepts.description: The current level of an Institution. Each level costs an amount of Bureaucracy depending on the Population size of your Incorporated States, and its effects scale with the level.…
concepts.name: Investment Level

concepts.description:
Reinvestment from Pops with Privately Owned Buildings is deposited into the Investment Pool, where Pops use it for Private Construction and purchasing Building Levels marked for Privatization.

Usually, … and … in … and … use the Investment Pool, but depending on your …, the Workforce can use it to expand their own Building.

A Country’s … restricts which Buildings can be built using the Investment Pool.

As Construction of such Buildings take place, the funds required to build them are deducted from the Investment Pool and deposited in the Treasury as an Investment Pool Transfer.
concepts.name: Investment Pool

concepts.description: When Money from the Treasury is used in the Construction of Buildings that may be funded by the Investment Pool under the Country’s current …, the Treasury is compensated by an equal transfer of funds from the Investment Pool.
concepts.name: Investment Pool Transfer

concepts.description:
A Country’s Involvement in a Strategic Region measures how strong their Interest is in the region.

You can increase Involvement in a Strategic Region by: 
• Stationing Fleets in the naval HQ
• Stationing Armies in the land HQ
• Having Fleets carrying out Orders in an adjacent Sea Node
• Having Armies fight on a Front in that Region
• Owning States in that Region
• Having Claims on States in that Region
• Moving your Capital State there
• Signing Treaties with Countries that are Local
• Engaging in Diplomatic Actions with Local Countries
concepts.name: Involvement

concepts.description: A State Region is considered Isolated from its Market if it is not connected by land to its Market Capital, and is not connected by land to a … that can make a Port Connection to its Market Capital. Isolated State Regions do not generate any Buy Orders and Sell Orders, nor is the Local Price of Goods affected by their Market Price.
concepts.name: Isolated State Region

concepts.description: Pops can be satisfied or dissatisfied with their jobs based on a number of factors such as their Standard of Living or Wage. This determines whether they are looking for new Employment or not.
concepts.name: Job Satisfaction

concepts.description: A Jobseeker is a Working Adult with negative Job Satisfaction who is not working in a Government Building or in a Building being Subsidized.
concepts.name: Jobseeker

concepts.description:
Journal Entries track ongoing events in your country. They can present opportunities or challenges, remind you of promises you have made, or warn of potential crises that may occur.

Journal Entries usually resolve and are removed from your Journal when they are considered Complete. Not all Journal Entries can be Completed - some can only Fail, Time Out, or will be removed under some condition.
concepts.name: Journal Entry

concepts.description: A Junior Partner in a Customs Union yields control of their Market to the Senior Partner. While the Junior Partner may continue to Trade with other Markets, they may not issue Embargoes or control Tariff levels. In exchange they collect a minor portion of the Market's Tariff income and their Industries benefit from participating in a more powerful and mature Market.
concepts.name: Junior Partner

concepts.description: How effective a Military Unit is at ensuring their opponent's Casualties end up unable to come back to fight another day. Increases the ratio of Casualties that end up killed (instead of Wounded). Kill Rate is countered by the enemy Military Unit's Recovery Rate.
concepts.name: Kill Rate

concepts.description: A type of Poll Tax collected from … and … employed in agricultural Buildings. Pops that pay Land Taxes do not pay Per Capita Taxes.
concepts.name: Land Taxes

concepts.description: The Landing Progress is equivalent to how much Occupation the invader has gained of the invaded State. If the Landing Progress reaches 100%, the Naval Invasion is successful and a Front will be established.
concepts.name: Landing Progress

concepts.description: Language Traits represent Languages deeply associated with a Culture. They also belong to a Trait Group, a broader family of similar Languages.
concepts.name: Language Trait

concepts.description: Laws sets the ground rules for how your Country operates and is governed. The effects of a Law are determined both by the base effects of the Law and those of any Amendments attached to it. Certain Laws enable Institutions that provide further control. For a Law to be able to be Enacted it must be Endorsed by at least one Interest Group In Government, supported by a current Political Movement, or have a positive Enactment Success chance for some other reason.
concepts.name: Law

concepts.description: A Law Group contains several Laws that affect aspects of the Country in different ways. Each Law Group can only have one Law active at a time.
concepts.name: Law Group

concepts.description: The Character who leads an Interest Group has a set of Character Traits that affect it, and a personal Ideology that is added to the Interest Group's Ideologies for as long as that Leader is in charge.
concepts.name: Leader

concepts.description: A Government’s Legitimacy measures how well the composition of the Interest Groups In Government fits with the Country’s Laws. The lower the Legitimacy, the longer the time between attempts to Enact new Laws. A Government with high Legitimacy is more Resistant to Coups. Raising or lowering Taxes also has an impact on Legitimacy.
concepts.name: Legitimacy

concepts.description: Power Blocs build up Leverage in Countries over time, by comparing their influence in the Country to that of other Power Blocs. Leverage share can be gained through different interactions, for example an active Diplomatic Pact or Treaty, and current Leverage will drift towards this share each week. Once enough Leverage Advantage has been accumulated over a Country, they can be invited to the Power Bloc.
concepts.name: Leverage

concepts.description:
The amount of Leverage a Power Bloc has over a Country compared to the other Power Blocs. If the value is +positive this Power Bloc has a Leverage Advantage meaning the most Leverage of all Power Blocs; if it is -negative this Power Bloc has a Leverage Disadvantage which means that some other Power Blocs currently has more than them, or the Country’s Unclaimed Leverage is higher.

In order for a Power Bloc Leader to invite a Country into their Power Bloc, Leverage Advantage must be positive and have reached a necessary threshold.
concepts.name: Leverage Advantage

concepts.description: A Power Bloc’s Leverage Share of a Country is the total Leverage the Power Bloc can have at any moment over that Country. Countries have a finite amount of Leverage that Power Blocs can project on them. This Leverage is divided up between all Power Blocs with any Leverage over this Country resulting in each Power Bloc’s Leverage Share. However, a certain amount of the Leverage may become Unclaimed based on the Country’s own Leverage Resistance.
concepts.name: Leverage Share

concepts.description: The demand for Autonomy in a Subject Country is measured by its Liberty Desire. The Subject will be loyal and stable while at low levels, while high levels of Liberty Desire could result in calls for greater self-governance, reduced obligations, or even armed revolt for independence.
concepts.name: Liberty Desire

concepts.description: Characters gain Life Experience over time and through special events. Life Experience influences the possibility of acquiring new Character Traits.
concepts.name: Life Experience

concepts.description:
The percentage or absolute number of individuals in a Pop who can read and write. Certain Professions demand higher Literacy than others, limiting the Qualifications for Pops in other Professions unless their Literacy is high enough. You can invest in your … in order to develop higher Literacy in your Population over time.

Pops will face an increasing penalty to Birth Rate proportional to their Literacy, up to the following:
…
concepts.name: Literacy

concepts.description:
Funds that the Treasury owes to the Country’s Building Owners.

Whenever the Treasury is running a negative balance, it will automatically increase its Loans unless it has sufficient Gold Reserves to cover it.

Interest is accrued on the Principal weekly. If the Principal ever exceeds the Country’s Credit, it goes into Default.
concepts.name: Loans

concepts.description:
A Journal Entry presented by a Political Lobby.

Fulfilling a Demand will increase Appeasement of the Lobby.
concepts.name: Lobby Demand

concepts.description:
A special Journal Entry offered by a Political Lobby supported by Interest Groups In Government.

These allow a special chance to achieve something normally not possible.
concepts.name: Lobby Opportunity

concepts.description:
A Country is Local to a Strategic Region if it satisfies any of the following conditions:
   • Has its Capital State in the Region
   • Has … or more Locality in the Region
   • Has … or more of its Incorporated States in the Region
concepts.name: Local Country

concepts.description: Local Goods are certain Goods that are not available in the wider Market outside the State where they are produced. Their price is fully determined by local Production and Consumption, with Market Price not factored in at all.
concepts.name: Local Good

concepts.description: The price of a Good in a State. It is determined by the local Consumption and Production, moderated by the Market Price depending on the State’s Market Access and Market Access Price Impact modifier. All transactions occur in the Local Price, with purchases and sales creating Buy and Sell Orders on the Market.
concepts.name: Local Price

concepts.description: A measure of how local a country is in a Strategic Region, which builds on a combination of the share of owned States, Population, and Gross Domestic Product in a Region
concepts.name: Locality

concepts.description:
The Lower Strata consist of Pops in Professions that work with their hands or do repetitive labor which require little to no Qualifications and result in low Wages.

Which Pops belong to this Strata depends on the Country’s Social Hierarchy.
concepts.name: Lower Strata

concepts.description:
Loyalist Individuals within a Pop are pleased with the state of their Country and are willing to defend it from dissident elements, both verbally and with violence if necessary. The Approval of Interest Groups supported by Loyalist Pops is improved.

Loyalists are created whenever a Pop's Standard of Living increases and due to decisions made during special events.

The opposite of a Loyalist is a Radical. Whenever a Radical would be created in a Pop that already has Loyalists, one Loyalist becomes Neutral instead.
concepts.name: Loyalist

concepts.description: The Loyalty of a Character measures how faithful they are to the sitting Government, and is affected by the Approval of their Interest Group as well as their personal Ideology. Disloyal Commanders may attempt to launch a Coup.
concepts.name: Loyalty

concepts.description: Magnates are wealthy Characters that own numerous estates or businesses and use their fortune to wield political power. Magnates possess a Holding in their Home State, and gain Prominence based on its Revenue.
concepts.name: Magnate

concepts.description: Countries of Major Powers Rank have established themselves as notable through their regional presence. While they are not yet strong enough to establish a truly global empire they can be a major local force to be reckoned with, and the most powerful among them may aspire to ascend to Great Power status.…
concepts.name: Major Power

concepts.description: Mandates are used to upgrade, switch or enact new Principles. Power Blocs gain Mandate Progress by having powerful Power Bloc Members and a high Cohesion value. Up to three Mandates can be stored.
concepts.name: Mandate

concepts.description: The progress towards the next Mandate. Power Blocs gain progress by having powerful Power Bloc Members and a high Cohesion value.
concepts.name: Mandate Progress

concepts.description: Maneuvers can be spent on taking actions in a Diplomatic Play, including claiming additional War Goals or Swaying other Countries to your side. The amount of Maneuvers you have is limited by your Rank.
concepts.name: Maneuver

concepts.description: The amount of … and … in a Military Unit. The greater the Manpower the more Casualties the Military Unit will be able to deal and take.
concepts.name: Manpower

concepts.description:
Marginalized Interest Groups have too little Clout to be politically noteworthy and cannot be included in the Government. A Marginalized Interest Group that is supported by at least … will be able to join a Party, and will cease being Marginalized once they do so. Their Interest Group Traits are deactivated for as long as they remain Marginalized.

Already Marginalized Interest Groups remain Marginalized for as long as their Clout is below …. Non-Marginalized Interest Groups that are not in a Party will become Marginalized once their Clout drops below …, unless they are already In Government in which case they do not become Marginalized until removed.

The Interest Group Traits of Interest Groups whose Clout is below … but are not Marginalized will have a … less effect than if they were merely Influential
concepts.name: Marginalized

concepts.description: An increase or decrease to the amount of marines a Ship can carry, affecting its ability to support Naval Invasions and other amphibious operations
concepts.name: Marine Capacity

concepts.description:
All States in the same Market will trade Goods with each other, unless they are Isolated. How well connected these States are with each other is measured by their Market Access. Markets may also trade with each other through the World Market.

Each Country either controls its own Market or participates in a different one via a Customs Union or Subject relationship.
concepts.name: Market

concepts.description: A measure of how well-connected a State is to the rest of its Market. It starts at 100% and is reduced proportionally whenever the State's Infrastructure Usage exceeds its Infrastructure. It impacts both how many Sell Orders and Buy Orders are generated due to the State's Production and Consumption, and also how much the Market Price affects the Local Price of Goods.
concepts.name: Market Access

concepts.description: Market Areas are parts of a Market that are connected via land or straits. There is always one World Market Hub per Market Area through which it conducts Trade with the World Market.
concepts.name: Market Area

concepts.description: The State that serves as the nexus of a Market, to which all other States in the Market must connect lest they become Isolated. Trade with the World Market is often, but not always, managed from the Market Capital. The Market Capital is often the same State as the Market Owner’s Capital State, but it is possible to keep these separate.…
concepts.name: Market Capital

concepts.description: Market Impact is how much of an effect the current balance of a Good (Buy Orders - Sell Orders) has on a Market. It is not determined solely by Market Price of a Good (being either cheap or expensive), but also takes into consideration the volume of that Good which circulates through the Market, affecting Pops and Industries.
concepts.name: Market Impact

concepts.description: A War Goal that can be claimed in a Diplomatic Play or as part of a Peace Deal. A Country forced to Open its Market immediately changes its … to … and may not change it again for … months. …
concepts.name: Market Opening

concepts.description: The Country that owns the market, either because it is the only participant or the Senior Partner in a Customs Union. Only the Market Owner may sign Trade Privileges and issue Embargoes.
concepts.name: Market Owner

concepts.description:
The price of a Good in the Market. It is based on Buy Orders and Sell Orders, and affect the Local Price of Goods in all participating States depending on their Market Access.

The degree to which the Market Price influences the Local Price is calculated by multiplying the Market Access with the State’s Market Access Price Impact modifier.
concepts.name: Market Price

concepts.description: The Market Share of each Country in a Market is determined by its Gross Domestic Product, with a bonus if they are the Market Owner. The higher a Country's Market Share the more Consumption Taxes they collect in the Market.
concepts.name: Market Share

concepts.description: A Mass Migration is the movement of Pops of a specific Culture in large numbers between two Countries. A Mass Migration Target may appear if there is a Trade connection between two Markets and the Cultural Turmoil of a specific Culture in the origin Country is at least …. A Country is more likely to have one of its States be selected as a Migration Target if it has a high Mass Migration Attraction.
concepts.name: Mass Migration

concepts.description:
A Country's Mass Migration Attraction indicates how likely it is to receive a Mass Migration compared to other Countries. It is largely based on the average Migration Attraction of Eligible States in the Country.

If a Country has fewer than … Eligible States it will receive an increasing penalty to its Mass Migration Attraction depending on how many Eligible States it has.
concepts.name: Mass Migration Attraction

concepts.description:
The Middle Strata consist of Pops with specialized Professions that are harder to gain Qualifications for. This provides them with more leverage on the labor market and thereby higher Wages.

Which Pops belong to this Strata depends on the Country’s Social Hierarchy.
concepts.name: Middle Strata

concepts.description:
The movement of Pops between States. Generally, Migration happens between States in the same Market, but it can also happen between Countries in different Markets in the case of Mass Migrations.

Migration flows from States with lower to higher Migration Attraction, with more people moving the higher the difference is. The Migration rate is also affected by factors like the available Infrastructure in a State.

Migration can only happen if there are Pops able and willing to Emigrate. Pops will only consider Emigrating if they are sufficiently Dissatisfied. For instance if their Standard of Living is lower than the average in their Market or if they are Unemployed.

Pops who arrive to a State with no other Pops of the same Culture, will form a Cultural Community and get a temporary penalty to their Acceptance.
concepts.name: Migration

concepts.description:
Migration Attraction is a State's ability to attract migrants. It is based primarily on the average Standard of Living among Pops in the State but can be modified by a number of other factors. Any Unemployment in the State will depress Migration Attraction. The value is compared against other States between which Migration may occur to determine in which direction migrants tend to flow.

Migration Attraction is also the primary factor used to determine a Country's Mass Migration Attraction.
concepts.name: Migration Attraction

concepts.description:
A State selected as a suitable target for a Mass Migration. Surrounding States may also see some degree of Immigration from a Mass Migration.

To be Eligible for Mass Migrations a state needs to be Incorporated, have at least … Arable Land and … Market Access. Additionally, the State cannot already be the target of a different Mass Migration and the Country's … and … Laws need to allow Migration to happen.
concepts.name: Migration Target

concepts.description: Military Access can be used to attack an enemy through the lands of other neutral Countries. It is secured by establishing an Ongoing Diplomatic Action with the neutral Country.
concepts.name: Military Access

concepts.description: An Ongoing Diplomatic Action established by one Country targeting another, where the first Country improves the fighting ability of the second's Formations
concepts.name: Military Assistance

concepts.description: Government Buildings used to train, maintain, and supply Battalions and Ships for the Country’s army and navy respectively. The Workforce of Military Buildings get paid according to the Military Wage.
concepts.name: Military Building

concepts.description: Goods Consumed by Military Buildings using funds from the Treasury.
concepts.name: Military Good

concepts.description: View the progress of ongoing Wars, construct Military Buildings, and recruit Commanders.
concepts.name: Military Lens

concepts.description: The upkeep of Slaves in the service of a Country’s military.
concepts.name: Military Slaves

concepts.description: Military Units are Battalions assigned to a Formation and perform military operations under the guidance of a General. Battalions are sub-divided into distinct groups: …. Units in the Default group are unlimited, while having more Special units than Default ones may incur an Organization penalty.
concepts.name: Military Unit

concepts.description: Military Units are categorized into Default Units and Special Units which possess different strengths and weaknesses. … is better suited for defending territory, while … is better at Occupation for example.
concepts.name: Military Unit Group

concepts.description: Within a Military Unit Group there are different types of Units. Most of the time, they are unlocked by technological advances and are better at fighting than the type they replace.
concepts.name: Military Unit Type

concepts.description: All Military Buildings pay their Workforce according to the same standardized Military Wage rate. This rate is based on the Normal Wage in the Country, with any adjustments set in the Budget panel.
concepts.name: Military Wage

concepts.description: Wages paid to Pops by Military Buildings. The rate is based on the Country’s Normal Wage. You can adjust it up and down in the Budget panel.
concepts.name: Military Wages

concepts.description: Minimum Expected Standard of Living is the lowest Standard of Living that a Pop is willing to tolerate. This number is based on whether the Pop is Lower Strata, Middle Strata, or Upper Strata and adjusted by Literacy, and can be modified by certain Technologies. If a Pop has a lower Standard of Living than the Minimum Expected they will gradually become more Radical. Pops with a Standard of Living above the Minimum Expected will still become more Radical each time their Standard of Living is reduced.
concepts.name: Minimum Expected Standard of Living

concepts.description: Countries of Minor Power Rank are pawns in the imperialist games of Major and Great Powers, who often use them as buffer Countries, Puppets, or captive Markets.…
concepts.name: Minor Power

concepts.description: A form of income that all Countries generate through the printing or casting of new Money. The greater a Country’s Gross Domestic Product, the more Money can be Minted without compromising the economy.
concepts.name: Minting

concepts.description: Mission Efficiency determines how efficiently a Fleet carries out its Naval Mission. It is based on the number of Regions assigned to the mission area and the fleet's current Presence.
concepts.name: Mission Efficiency

concepts.description: An Army can be configured with any number of Mobilization Options while in peacetime. Each Option applies a cost in Goods and an effect for all Battalions in the Army while it is Mobilized.
concepts.name: Mobilization Option

concepts.description: Mobilizing an Army will immediately begin the process of Mobilization for all Battalions assigned to it. A Mobilized Army will automatically stand down once the Country is no longer at War. Early Demobilization while in active warfare is possible, but takes time and a substantial cost.
concepts.name: Mobilize Army

concepts.description: Battalions in a Mobilized Army immediately start Mobilizing at a rate based on the Infrastructure of their State, better Infrastructure means more Battalions may Mobilize at once. Mobilized and Mobilizing Battalions consume more Military Goods based on their Army's Mobilization Options, but are fully prepared to follow any of their Army's Generals into Battle.
concepts.name: Mobilize Battalion

concepts.description: Any adjustment of a value away from its norm is considered a Modifier. These can be indefinite or Timed, and their origin can always be sourced back to something like a Law, Technology, Institution, Building, Character Trait, or even an option selected during a special event. Values adjusted by Modifiers all have tooltips that explain the full list of sources and their values.
concepts.name: Modifier

concepts.description: The success of a Party’s Election campaign. Momentum increases the number of Votes a Party gains on Election day, and is nullified thereafter. Momentum can be affected by random chance, special events, and the Popularity of its Party Leader.
concepts.name: Momentum

concepts.description: Money makes the world go 'round. It is used to pay for Government Wages and Bureaucracy production, Construction materials, industry Subsidies, … for your Shipping Lanes, and last but probably not least, your military. You gain Money by Taxing your Pops and enforcing Tariffs. Excess Money in your Treasury balance is used to pay off your Loans or stockpile gold in your Gold Reserves. Insufficient Money increases your Loans towards your Credit Limit, which is determined by how much Money is in your Buildings' Cash Reserves.
concepts.name: Money

concepts.description: A Monopoly on a Building gives its owner exclusive Building rights of that Industry. It can either be a Company Monopoly or a Country Monopoly.
concepts.name: Monopoly

concepts.description: Buildings unique to a certain State that can perform a variety of functions, often conferring Prestige.
concepts.name: Monument

concepts.description:
A Military Unit’s Morale measures how much of its remaining Manpower is ready for Battle. In each round of combat, some of the remaining Manpower will become Demoralized for the remainder of the Battle and unable to take offensive action. As all Military Units reach a critical threshold of low Morale the Commander will retreat, leaving the other side victorious.

After a Battle, Military Units will regain their Morale at a steady rate depending on the Supply of their Formation.
concepts.name: Morale

concepts.description: The amount of damage a Military Unit inflicts on its enemy's Morale
concepts.name: Morale Damage

concepts.description:
Movement Activism is the percentage of Supporting Pops willing to actively push for a Political Movement’s agenda. It determines how many Radicals are generated by the Movement each week and how close the Movement is to becoming Insurrectionary. If it is already Insurrectionary, it determines the max progress the Revolution can reach.

Luckily, we are able to predict how a Political Movement’s Activism will shift. If the prediction is Protesting (…) or above, the Movement has a high risk of becoming Insurrectionary. If the prediction is Militant (100%) and the Support is enough, a Civil War is imminent since the progress of the Revolution or Secession can now reach 100%.

If the Activism is at least … (…), the Movement will increase the Enactment Success and Stall chances of the Endorsed and Opposed Laws in the Core Movement Ideology based on the Support.

If the Activism is at least … (…), a number of Supporting Pops will become Radicalized each month, and certain Movements will begin to generate Obstinance in States with Supporting Pops.

Activism thresholds: 
…
concepts.name: Movement Activism

concepts.description:
Political Movements will Pressure Interest Groups based on the percentage of Political Strength from Supporting Pops. The Interest Group is considered Pressured if the Pressure is above …. Then the Political Movement’s Character Ideologies will become possible for new Leaders of that Interest Group.

All Pops in an Interest Group have varying Political Strength which sums up to the Interest Group’s total Political Strength. The percentage of this total Political Strength, represented by Pops who are Supporting a Political Movement, is what defines the Movement Pressure. Pops with high Political Strength will have higher leverage to influence their Interest Groups with their Political Movement’s Ideologies and beliefs.
concepts.name: Movement Pressure

concepts.description: If a Country meets certain requirements, such as owning land in specific State Regions and/or having discovered a certain Society Technology, they may be able to form a new Country of a higher Country Tier. The possible Countries are listed in the Nation Formation tab in the Journal panel.
concepts.name: Nation Formation

concepts.description: A Culture which reaches … Fervor has a chance to start a National Awakening. Cultures with an active National Awakening will gain additional Fervor whilst it is active, and Political Movements with this Culture will have greater Pop Attraction.
concepts.name: National Awakening

concepts.description: A National Hero is a general who has won a battle against a state that is not Brazilian, and been hailed as a hero in the event 'A New National Hero'.
concepts.name: National Hero

concepts.description:
A Building that is not fully Nationally Owned can be Nationalized by the owner of the State the Building is in.

Nationalizing Privately Owned Levels may Radicalize the Pops that own the Building, especially if you do not offer Money as compensation.

A Foreign Investment can also be Nationalized, if the owning Country is no longer allowed to make Foreign Investments.

The availability and cost of Nationalization depends on your ….
concepts.name: Nationalize

concepts.description:
A Building Level that is owned by the Government of a Country.

Nationally Owned Levels pay out Government Dividends to the Country that owns them. While Nationally Owned Levels provide Money directly to the Government, they cost Bureaucracy and have reduced benefits from Economy of Scale.

Building Levels built by Government Construction become Nationally Owned, and all Government Buildings are fully Nationally Owned.

A Building can be Nationalized to turn their Building Levels to Nationally Owned, or become Privately Owned via Privatization.
concepts.name: Nationally Owned

concepts.description: A type of Diplomatic Play that can occur if the Tension between a colonizer and a Decentralized Nation rises to Volatile level. In this Play, the Decentralized Nation will mobilize its warriors and attempt to seize the Colony from the colonizer.
concepts.name: Native Uprising

concepts.description:
When two Commanders encounter each other and come into conflict during a War, they and their Ships will clash in an attempt to inflict Casualties and sink each other' Ships. The side whose Ships have all been destroyed or disengaged will withdraw, leaving the other side victorious.

Naval Battles take place in Sea Nodes when one Admiral intercepts another due to conflicting Orders. The winner leaves their opponent damaged and forces them to return to port for repairs, leaving them unable to execute their Order for a time.
concepts.name: Naval Battle

concepts.description: Naval Battles are affected by a Naval Battle Condition that influences everyone involved in the battle. Which Condition applies depends on a number of factors, which often includes any Harvest Condition affecting the location of the Naval Battle.
concepts.name: Naval Battle Condition

concepts.description: Naval Hostilities is a state of hostility between two Countries that permits hostile naval actions without a formal War. Fleets may engage in Battles and enforce Blockades against countries with which they have Naval Hostilities.
concepts.name: Naval Hostilities

concepts.description:
A maritime invasion of a coastal State, coordinated between a Fleet and an Army. The Fleet keeps the waters off the coast clear to ensure the Army can land safely, while the Army executes a series of land Battles to win Occupation in the targeted State.

The controller of the targeted State can defend against the Naval Invasion by positioning their own Fleets in the affected Sea Node or stationing a Mobilized Army in the invaded State.
concepts.name: Naval Invasion

concepts.description: Naval Invasion Support is a comparison of the amount of the Ships you have assigned to naval invasion to the amount of Battalions taking part in that invasion. Each invading Battalion requires a Ship to avoid any negative penalties upon landing.
concepts.name: Naval Invasion Support

concepts.description: Fleets can be assigned to Naval Missions to determine what they should be focused on. A Mission takes place in a set of connected Sea Nodes and has different effects depending on the type of the Mission.
concepts.name: Naval Mission

concepts.description: The maximum number of Sea Regions that can be assigned to a Mission. This limit is determined by the Commander Rank of the assigned Admiral.
concepts.name: Naval Mission Area Limit

concepts.description: The Power Projection derived from a Country’s navy.
concepts.name: Naval Power Projection

concepts.description:
Negotiate with an Interest Group during Enactment to convince them to change their stance on the currently Enacting Law. An Interest Group’s willingness to Negotiate is determined by their Amenability. The higher Amenability they have the friendlier and more willing they will be to Negotiate.

Indifferent Interest Groups must be In Government to be Negotiated with while Opposing Interest Groups can be Negotiated with when In Opposition.

Convincing an Interest Group to move from Opposing to Indifferent can be just as effective has convincing them to move from Indifferent to Endorsing.
concepts.name: Negotiation

concepts.description: Two Countries are considered to be Neighbors if they share a land border or if they both own coastal States that connect to the same Sea Node.
concepts.name: Neighbors

concepts.description:
Neutral Individuals within a Pop are neither Radical or Loyal towards their Country. However, they are only one negative or positive step away from becoming Radical or Loyal.

Whenever a Radical would be created in a Pop that already has Loyalists, one Loyalist becomes Neutral instead. All Individuals in a Pop needs to be either Neutral or already Radical for a Radical to be created. Vice versa when a Loyalist would be created.
concepts.name: Neutral

concepts.description: All AI-controlled Countries involved in a Diplomatic Play have a level of Neutrality based on their internal conditions and their general level of interest in the participants of the play. The higher their Neutrality, the more difficult it will be to convince that Country to get involved in the play.
concepts.name: Neutrality

concepts.description:
Some Articles may come with specific duties attached that will adversely affect the Treaty if Contravened. An Article is considered Non-Fulfilled if consecutively Contravened up to the maximum number of allowed Contraventions for that Article.

Consequences of Non-Fulfillment may include subjecting the Contravening Country to compensation payments, as well as freezing or outright breaking the Treaty.

If a Treaty is frozen, the Contravening Country still pays and fulfills whatever they can from their Articles, but receives nothing in return.
concepts.name: Non-Fulfillment

concepts.description: Notifications that does not appear anywhere in the user interface.
concepts.name: None

concepts.description: Alerts/important actions that does not appear anywhere in the user interface.
concepts.name: None

concepts.description: The baseline Wage in a Country which many Buildings take into account. Government Wages and Military Wages are based on the Normal Wage. It is determined from the average Wages paid by Industries across Incorporated States.
concepts.name: Normal Wage

concepts.description: One Country can become Obligated to another as a result of agreements made during Diplomatic Plays or when one Country buys out another's Loans. While Obligated to a Country you are unable to start Diplomatic Plays against them or even join a Play on the other side as them. The other Country may use an Obligation they hold over you to force you into a Diplomatic Pact or Treaty, or may absolve it to Sway you into supporting them in a Diplomatic Play or increase Relations with you.
concepts.name: Obligation

concepts.description: An Observing player has full access to the user interface and insight into what is happening in the game, but cannot make any gameplay changes.
concepts.name: Observer Mode

concepts.description: A Culture can be Obsessed with specific Goods. Pops of that Culture will spend significantly more on Goods they are Obsessed with compared to other Goods in the same Pop Needs category.
concepts.name: Obsession

concepts.description:
Obstinance represents Pops supporting a Cultural Movement or Religious Movement within a State passively refusing to comply with a Country's Institutions. Obstinance is caused by the Movement Activism of an applicable Movement exceeding Protesting (…). The amount of Obstinance is equal to the fraction of the State's Workforce that are members of an Obstinate Political Movement.

The presence of Obstinance in a state inflicts a number of negative local status effects on a State, such as reduced Assimilation, Tax Collection, Conscription, and Institution impact.
concepts.name: Obstinance

concepts.description: How fully employed a Building is, which also determines how much of its maximum Productive capacity is utilized. If the Building has room to hire a larger Workforce, it will always try to do so. If its hiring is limited by the Wage it can offer, it will increase Wages for as long as its Balance remains positive.
concepts.name: Occupancy

concepts.description: Any Provinces the Country owns that are currently part of an enemy Theater are considered Occupied. Occupation contributes to War Exhaustion. Occupying a War Goal you hold on an enemy is usually required to bring their War Support into the negatives.
concepts.name: Occupation

concepts.description: A Military Unit’s fighting ability in Battle while advancing into enemy territory.
concepts.name: Offense

concepts.description: A participant in a Diplomatic Play can Offer Support to the Initiator or Target in a Diplomatic Play. This works exactly like a Sway, with the exception that it is the potential supporter that sets the terms of what they are willing to be Swayed with, but does not cost any Maneuvers for either side.
concepts.name: Offer Support

concepts.description: A type of Diplomatic Pact that can be both initiated and ended at will, with no approval required nor costs incurred by the target Country.
concepts.name: Ongoing Diplomatic Action

concepts.description: The Opening Moves phase is the first phase of a Diplomatic Play. In this phase the Target gets to set their primary War Goal, and both Initiator and Target can claim additional War Goals using Maneuvers.
concepts.name: Opening Moves

concepts.description:
Commanders can be given Orders that cause them to pursue different military objectives depending on their current location. All Commanders have a few basic Orders, but their Character Traits may add special Orders for that Commander to use.

Basic General orders are:
…
concepts.name: Order

concepts.description:
A Formation with low Organization will be less effective in Battle in a variety of ways. Organization starts out low when a Formation is first created, but will increase over time while the Formation is not traveling. Organization is limited if you have too low Command Limit for all your Military Units or if your Formation has more Special Units than Default Units.

Organization can also be impacted temporarily when switching Mobilization Options on or off, and when transferring Military Units between Mobilized Armies with different sets of Mobilization Options.

A Formation with low Organization will suffer increasing penalties the lower the value is.

For an Army, these penalties go up to the following effects:
…

For a Fleet, the penalties are at most the following:
…
concepts.name: Organization

concepts.description: The dominant Country in a Subject relationship, who derive a number of benefits from the Diplomatic Pact while (usually) having to pay Influence for it.
concepts.name: Overlord

concepts.description: A type of Diplomatic Action that Overlords can issue against their Subjects.
concepts.name: Overlord Action

concepts.description: The Parent Law of an Amendment determines the Stance of an Ideology towards the Amendment. Each Interest Group will then Endorse or Oppose an Amendment depending on their Ideologies.
concepts.name: Parent Law

concepts.description: A Party is a political entity that participates in Election. They consist of one or more Interest Groups whose Ideologies are at least somewhat compatible. These Interest Groups are empowered by the Votes the Party has won proportional to their Clout. Individual Interest Groups cannot be included in Government without the rest of their Party members.
concepts.name: Party

concepts.description: The Leader of the Interest Group in the Party with the most Clout is considered the Party Leader. The Leader acts as a Party Whip.
concepts.name: Party Leader

concepts.description: The Leader of the Interest Group in the Party with the most Clout is considered the Party Leader. The Leader acts as a Party Whip.
concepts.name: Party Leaders

concepts.description: The Party Whip keeps the rest of their Party member's Ideologies in check. When In Government, the Party Whip partially overrides the ideological Law stances on the other Interest Groups in the Party for the purposes of calculating Ideological Incompatibility. The Party Leader acts as the Whip.
concepts.name: Party Whip

concepts.description: When a War Leader wish to end a War they may offer a Peace Deal. The deal must be agreed to by all negotiating Countries remaining in the War to take effect. To increase the chance the Peace Deal will be agreed to, the War Leader is allowed to include or exclude proposed War Goals from both sides.
concepts.name: Peace Deal

concepts.description: A type of Poll Tax collected from all Pops except ….
concepts.name: Per Capita Taxes

concepts.description: Two Countries with the … Law may be joined together in a Personal Union (Subject), a Subject Type where the Overlord’s Ruler is the Head of State in both Countries. The subject cannot start their own Diplomatic Plays, yet are forced to join their Overlord's Wars. The Diplomatic Pact will break if the Overlord abolishes the Monarchy.
concepts.name: Personal Union

concepts.description: Money collected from the proactive redistribution of Goods on the high seas by Piracy or Privateer Naval Missions.
concepts.name: Piracy

concepts.description: View Interest Groups and Incorporated States, construct Government Buildings, issue Decrees, and manage matters of domestic political importance to your Country.
concepts.name: Political Lens

concepts.description:
A Political Lobby is a collection of Interest Groups either opposing or endorsing a certain Country.

The Interest Groups in the Lobby gain Approval based on the Appeasement of the Political Lobby.

Lobbies make it easier or harder to perform Diplomatic Actions against their target Country, by affecting Influence cost, and if the Country will accept. Lobbies in Subjects which target their Overlord affect Liberty Desire. These effects are scaled by the Clout of the Lobby.

…Lobbies may form randomly when a Diplomatic Catalyst happens, or when a Country is Funding Lobbies in another.
concepts.name: Political Lobby

concepts.description:
A Political Movement is driven by Pops Supporting it based on its Core Movement Ideology. Their Support comes in varying degrees of Movement Activism dependent on how many Pops are engaged or angry enough on the matter. Agitators can also join and Support a Movement, increasing the Activism based on their Popularity. If enough Pops are Supporting and the Activism is high enough, the Movement may become Insurrectionary, depending on the Laws in the Core Movement Ideology and the type of Movement. An Insurrectionary Movement may in turn lead to a Civil War breaking out.

Political Movements will exert Movement Pressure on Interest Groups based on the percentage of Political Strength from Supporting Pops.

Movements both affect Laws and vice versa. If the Movement Activism is at least … (…), the Movement will increase the Enactment Success and Stall chances of the Endorsed and Opposed Laws in the Core Ideology based on the Support. Similarly, if a Movement is at least … (…) and a Law, either Endorsed or Opposed by the Core Ideology, is being Enacted, the Activism cannot drop below … (…).
concepts.name: Political Movement

concepts.description:
The Support of a Political Movement is based on the Political Strength of its supporting Pops as well as the Popularity and Character Traits of any supporting Agitators. A Political Movement with at least … (…) Activism increases the Enactment Success chance if you pursue a Law they desire, or increases the Stall chance if they oppose it. This increased chance is directly based on the Support. Should the Political Movement lead to a Insurrection, Political Movement Support will determine how many States it will start with.

Support thresholds: 
…
concepts.name: Political Movement Support

concepts.description:
The degree of power a Pop, and consequently the Interest Groups it supports, have over the Country’s politics. It is derived from its supporting Pops' Wealth. Pops who live in Unincorporated States have much less Political Strength, while Pops in the Capital State have more.

Pops distribute their Political Strength to the Interest Groups it supports proportionate to how many of its members support it. If an Interest Group is a member of a Party, they also gain Political Strength from the Votes that Party received in the last Election. An Interest Group's Clout is equal to their share of the Country's total Political Strength.
concepts.name: Political Strength

concepts.description:
The part of a Pop that does not support an Interest Group is called Politically Unaligned. This is often due to low Literacy or Standard of Living. Politically Unaligned parts of Pops do not participate in the political process and any Political Strength they possess is wasted.

The opposite of this is Politically Aligned. Which means the Pop is part of one of your Country’s Interest Groups and the Pop's Political Strength is attributed to that Interest Group.

Characters below the age of … are usually Politically Unaligned.
concepts.name: Politically Unaligned/Aligned

concepts.description: A Character that is actively engaged in the day-to-day politics of their Interest Group. Politicians are eligible to become its next Leader even if their Prominence is below ….
concepts.name: Politician

concepts.description: A flat Tax collected on every Working Adult it applies to. Since Poll Taxes do not scale with the Pop's income it tends to impact the Lower Strata the most.
concepts.name: Poll Taxes

concepts.description:
The Pollution Impact on a State Region indicates how severe the effects of the total Generated Pollution by buildings in that State Region are. The more Arable Land a State Region has, the lower the impact of the Generated Pollution.

A highly polluted State Region will also affect its neighboring states, although at a reduced rate. If a neighboring state already has a higher Pollution Impact due to its own buildings or other neighboring states, only the highest Pollution Impact has an effect.

The effects of Pollution Impact can increase up to:
…
…
concepts.name: Pollution Impact

concepts.description: The world's population are organized into Pops, groups of individuals who work in the same Building as a certain Profession, and share the same Culture and Religion. They use the Income they earn to buy Goods to satisfy their Needs, which decides their Wealth and Standard of Living. They can support Interest Groups and Political Movements, or be Politically Unaligned. A Pop has a number of Working Adults and a number of Dependents. Some number of them are Literate, and they might have a number of either Loyalists or Radicals.
concepts.name: Pop

concepts.description:
The net number of Individuals a Pop gains or loses over time is governed by its Birth Rate and Mortality. Both metrics are governed by Standard of Living and modified by factors such as disease, dangerous working conditions, beneficial Institutions, and available living space.

External changes to a Pop's size due to e.g. Migration or Casualties of War are not considered Pop Growth.
concepts.name: Pop Growth

concepts.description: At the end of each week, Pops receive an Income based on the size of their Workforce and the current Wage offered to them, plus the size of their Dependents and the amount of Dependent Income they collect. This Income is spent on Pop Needs which impact the Pop's Wealth.
concepts.name: Pop Income

concepts.description: Pops spend their income on Goods to fulfill their Needs. The higher their Wealth the more Goods it will purchase. Pops gain more diverse and luxurious Needs as their Wealth increases. A given Need can often be satisfied by a variety of Goods via Goods Substitution. If the Pop has money left over after its Needs have been fulfilled their Wealth will increase. The inverse is also true: if the Pop cannot afford their Needs they will still purchase them, and the shortfall reduces their Wealth.
concepts.name: Pop Needs

concepts.description:
Determines how the Profit of Building Levels that are Privately Owned by its Workforce is distributed.

The Dividends are given to each Pops as Pop Income, depending on the size of their share compared to the rest of the Workforce.

The Pop is also considered to own that proportion of the Building's current Cash Reserves.

This is the main source of income for … and …, as they are considered part of the Workforce of … and …, respectively.
concepts.name: Pop Ownership Share

concepts.description:
The Popularity of a Character measures the willingness of Pops to follow them. 

Popularity affects Prominence and can have different effects depending on the Character's Role: 
• Agitators: affects chance of Pops joining their Political Movement 
• Rulers: adds or takes away Authority 
• Admirals/Generals: affects chance of launching a successful Coup 
• Interest Group Leaders: affects Interest Group Attraction 
• Party Leaders: affects Party Momentum during Elections 
• Executives: affects Prosperity
concepts.name: Popularity

concepts.description: Customized Notifications that pop up in the middle of the screen and have to be manually closed. This option is only available if the Notification Type has a customized popup panel specified.
concepts.name: Popup

concepts.description: A Shipping Lane connecting one or several States otherwise unreachable overland to the Market Capital, ensuring Market Access to remote regions. Port Connections require a … in both ends. The shipping cost of a Port Connection is dependent on the total Infrastructure Usage of the States it's connecting.
concepts.name: Port Connection

concepts.description:
A Country’s maximum potential Battalions is the sum of the its Potential Regular Battalions and Potential Conscript Battalions.

Potential Regular Battalions: the number of Battalions the Country's currently constructed … are able to support

Potential Conscript Battalions: the number of Conscript Battalions the Country's …s would create if Conscription had been activated across all States
concepts.name: Potential Battalions

concepts.description: Power Blocs are multinational associations, led by a Great Power, Major Power, or Unrecognized Major Power, that grant powerful effects to Power Bloc Leaders and Power Bloc Members. They serve the Bloc Leader in building their sphere of influence by building up Leverage Advantage in Countries to make them join the Power Bloc.
concepts.name: Power Bloc

concepts.description: Money collected from a Power Bloc Member or remitted to the Power Bloc Leader
concepts.name: Power Bloc Budget

concepts.description: A Great Power, Major Power, or Unrecognized Major Power that leads a Power Bloc. They tend to benefit more from Power Blocs than regular Power Bloc Members.
concepts.name: Power Bloc Leader

concepts.description: A member of a Power Bloc, this includes the Bloc Leader except when calculating Mandate Progress. Although, Non-leader Bloc Members tend to benefit less from Power Blocs than their Power Bloc Leaders.
concepts.name: Power Bloc Member

concepts.description: A Power Bloc’s Rank is solely based on its Bloc Members total Prestige compared to all other Power Blocs.
concepts.name: Power Bloc Rank

concepts.description: The total capability of a Country’s military forces, based on an average of the Offense and Defense of all their Military Units. It forms the basis for the amount of Prestige that a Country gains from its army and navy, and also affects how powerful other Countries perceive them to be when deciding to start or take sides in a Diplomatic Play.
concepts.name: Power Projection

concepts.description: A Power Struggle is the attempt of a Power Bloc Member to take leadership from the current Power Bloc Leader. It automatically triggers if a Non-leader Power Bloc Member has … more Prestige than the Power Bloc Leader. If they uphold at least … more Prestige for … months, they become the new Power Bloc Leader.
concepts.name: Power Struggle

concepts.description:
The amount of Clout an Interest Group has decides whether it is Powerful, Influential, or Marginalized. A Powerful Interest Group's Interest Group Traits will have a … greater effect than if they were merely Influential.

Interest Groups are considered Powerful while their Clout is above ….
concepts.name: Powerful

concepts.description: The Presence of a Fleet affects how effectively its Admirals carry out their Orders. Presence builds up over time while a Fleet is stationary in a Sea Node.
concepts.name: Presence

concepts.description:
The Presidencies are the highest level administrative units of colonial India. There are three Presidencies, with borders delineated by Geographic Regions.

Bengal Presidency
Geographic Regions: …, …, and ….

Bombay Presidency
Geographic Regions: ….

Madras Presidency
Geographic Regions: ….
concepts.name: Presidency

concepts.description:
Presidency Stability is a metric for the level of unrest within one of the three Presidencies of colonial India.

The stability of a Presidency falls within one of four brackets: 
Critical: …-…
Low: …-…
Medium: …-…
High: …-…

The following conditions in a Presidency decrease its stability: 
• States in Turmoil in the Presidency
• Subjects with high Liberty Desire in the Presidency

The following conditions in the East India Company decrease stability: 
• Low Approval of …
• High Taxes in the East India Company
• Low Military Wages in the East India Company
• … leaders in Government
• Not having the … Law
• Not having the … Law
• Events and other effects 

The following conditions increase the stability of a Presidency: 
• States with Loyalists in the Presidency
• Subjects with low Liberty Desire in the Presidency

The following conditions in the East India Company increase stability: 
• Native Indian Interest Groups In Government
• High Approval of …
• Low Taxes in the East India Company
• High Military Wages in the East India Company
• Events and other effects
concepts.name: Presidency Stability

concepts.description: Your Rank is determined by comparing your Prestige to all other Countries in the world. Prestige originates primarily from how impressive your economy is as measured by your Gross Domestic Product, how much Power Projection your military forces generate, and your Country Tier. It can also be affected by other factors such as your … and Monuments, and if you are a world leader in the production of a certain Good.
concepts.name: Prestige

concepts.description:
A Good that is considered prestigious and to be of superior quality. Prestige Goods are produced by some Companies that have a high enough Prosperity. Being a top producer of Prestige Goods grants significant Prestige.

Additionally, Prestige Goods grant the following benefits:
• Increased Consumption by Pops relative to other Goods
• Increased Trade Advantage for Exports
• Increased Throughput for Industries which use them as Input Goods
• Increased Offense and Defense for Military Units that consume them as supplies
concepts.name: Prestige Good

concepts.description: The Culture or Cultures a Nation-State is primarily associated with. If a Country forms a different Country its Primary Cultures may change, but will otherwise remain the same.…
concepts.name: Primary Cultures

concepts.description: Primary Demands are War Goals that will be enforced on the opposing side of a Diplomatic Play if they decide to back down. The first War Goal added on each side is always a Primary Demand, as are any War Goals added against the leader of the opposing side through Swaying.
concepts.name: Primary Demand

concepts.description: A Primary Principle Group is dependent on a Power Bloc’s selected Central Identity Pillar. A Power Bloc must always have at least one Principle from a Primary Group to have a stable Cohesion. Mandating higher-tier Principles from Primary Groups (tier II and III) strengthens the Cohesion further.
concepts.name: Primary Principle Group

concepts.description: A Princely State is a state under the rule of a native Indian monarch subordinate to a European colonial power. They possess greatly different degrees of prominence within the Indian imperial system, but all are generally subject to a similar diplomatic arrangement.
concepts.name: Princely State

concepts.description: The total size of Loans the Treasury has accrued, not including the Interest it owes. If the Principal exceeds your Credit you will go into Default.
concepts.name: Principal

concepts.description: Principles belong to a Principle Group and are bestowing different kinds of effects on Power Blocs and Power Bloc Member. They cost Mandates to enact and can be upgraded.
concepts.name: Principle

concepts.description: Groups of three tiers of Principles that support the same theme.
concepts.name: Principle Group

concepts.description:
A Private Construction is a Building that is being expanded on the orders of private actors.

It is always funded by the Investment Pool and cannot be can be reprioritized or removed from the Construction Queue.

The resulting Building Levels become Privately Owned
concepts.name: Private Construction

concepts.description:
A Building Level that is owned by Pops. These Pops are either the Workforce of the Building itself, or the Workforce of … and … (mainly … and …).

Privately Owned Levels pay out Dividends to the Pops that own them.

Building Levels built by Private Construction become Privately Owned.

A Building can be Nationalized to turn their Building Levels to Nationally Owned, or become Privately Owned via Privatization.
concepts.name: Privately Owned

concepts.description: A Building that is Nationally Owned can be put up for sale, allowing Pops to purchase it and make it Privately Owned through the Investment Pool. Whether Privatization is available depends on your ….
concepts.name: Privatize

concepts.description:
A Privy Purse is the personal income of a Monarch. In the context of …, it represents the pension paid to the former ruler of a Princely State annexed by another Country using a The Federation of India Journal Entry.

The Privy Purse Payments modifier will be added upon annexing any Princely State with this Journal Entry, and will be updated upon each subsequent annexation. The Privy Purse payments will add National Expenses equivalent to 0.01% Gross Domestic Product times the number of Princely States annexed using this Journal Entry
concepts.name: Privy Purse

concepts.description: The amount of a Good produced by a Building to be sold for Revenue.
concepts.name: Production

concepts.description: View States and construct Production Buildings.
concepts.name: Production Lens

concepts.description:
Production Methods determine how Buildings operate. They impact

- The Input Goods the Building must purchase to operate
- The Output Goods the Building produces and sells
- The distribution of Professions among its Workforce

Production Methods can also have other effects, such as the generation of Modifiers. Production Methods are organized in groups, in which only one can be active at a time. You can switch which Production Method is active in each group as long as you meet the Technology and Law requirement for it.
concepts.name: Production Method

concepts.description:
Productivity is a relative measure of how much economic value a Building generates per employee per year. It is calculated by taking the current weekly Revenue generated from Production, subtracting the expenses incurred from Consumption, dividing by the total Workforce, and multiplying by 52 (weeks / year).

( Revenue - Material Expenses ) / Total Employees

The difference between Productivity and Average Annual Wage is the Building's weekly Balance, also known as Profit.

Companies also have a Productivity rating, which is equal to the average Productivity of all their associated Building levels.
concepts.name: Productivity

concepts.description: A Pop’s Profession determines which role they perform in their Building, how large of a Wage they collect from it, and whether or not they get Pop Ownership Shares in it. It also impacts which Interest Group they're likely to support, how likely they are to remain Politically Unaligned, and whether they are considered Lower Strata, Middle Strata, or Upper Strata. To switch Professions, a Pop must have the appropriate Qualifications.
concepts.name: Profession

concepts.description: The Prominence of a Character measures their level of influence in the Country’s political machine and affects the chance that a Character will be selected as the next leader of their Interest Group. Characters whose Prominence is at least … also contribute to the Political Strength of their Interest Group and may be selected as its next Leader.
concepts.name: Prominence

concepts.description:
A Pronunciamento is the final stage of a Coup, in which a Commander declares opposition to the sitting Government and rallies their forces to support them. When a Pronunciamento occurs, the Coup Resistance of the sitting Government is compared to the Coup Strength of Commander executing the Coup.

If the Coup Strength of the Commander is less than the Coup Resistance of the Government, or if the Coup is triggered by a Character Interaction, the Government will have a chance to defend itself against the Coup. The …'s chance of successfully defending itself is determined by the ratio of Coup Resistance to the aforementioned factors.
