A successful Pronunciamento will cause the overthrow of the Government. A failed Pronunciamento will result in increased Radicalism, and negative repercussions for the coupist Commander.
concepts.name: Pronunciamento

concepts.description:
Companies have a Prosperity score which depends on their Productivity and number of employed Building levels, among other factors. When a Company reaches … Prosperity, it will be considered Prosperous and activate a bonus Modifier for its Country.
If the Prosperity of a Prosperous company falls below … it will no longer be considered Prosperous and its bonus Modifier will be deactivated.
concepts.name: Prosperity

concepts.description: A Protectorate (Subject) is an autonomous Subject Type able to start their own Diplomatic Plays.
concepts.name: Protectorate

concepts.description: Subdivisions of States, each with its own Terrain. Provinces are transferred between States during Colonization, and can be temporarily transferred between Theaters during War as the outcome of Battles.
concepts.name: Province

concepts.description: Recognized Powers may turn a weaker Country into their Puppet (Subject). A Puppet is a Subject Type that cannot start their own Diplomatic Plays yet are forced to join their Overlord’s Wars, and must also pay 30% of their Treasury income to their Overlord each week. A Puppet's Rank cannot increase to match or exceed their Overlord's, and their Overlord may target them with the Annexation Diplomatic Play.
concepts.name: Puppet

concepts.description: Pops develop the Qualifications necessary to change into another Profession over time. If their current attributes match those of the Profession, or if they currently work in a related field, they will develop Qualifications for it sooner. Literacy, Wealth, and Acceptance Status are common deciding factors.
concepts.name: Qualifications

concepts.description:
Radical Individuals within a Pop are disillusioned with the state of their Country. The presence of Radicals in a State contributes to Turmoil, and the Radicalism of Pops contributes to Movement Activism. The Approval of Interest Groups supported by Radical Pops will also be impacted.

Radicals are created when a Pop’s Standard of Living falls below their Minimum Expected Standard of Living, whenever a Pop’s Standard of Living decreases, and due to decisions made during special events. Pops suffering from a low Acceptance Status increase these negative effects further. Radicals are also created in Pops that support Political Movements whose demands go unfulfilled, and when Pops are fired from a Building’s Workforce (particularly if they had a large Pop Ownership Share).

The opposite of a Radical is a Loyalist. Whenever a Loyalist would be created in a Pop that already has Radicals, one Radical becomes Neutral instead.
concepts.name: Radical

concepts.description: When an Interest Group's Approval is below …, it is said to be Radicalized. A Radicalized Interest Group is likely to become Insurrectionary, or stage a Coup against the sitting Government.
concepts.name: Radicalized Interest Group

concepts.description:
Raiding is income derived from the theft, pillage and plunder of neighboring lands over time. With little arable land, Montenegro must rely on Raiding and Russian Aid to survive. 

Our income from raiding is dependent on our Raiding Fervor multiplied by our army's Power Projection. +… is the most we can possibly earn from raiding.
concepts.name: Raiding

concepts.description:
Raiding Fervor represents how often the tribes are permitted to raid.

In addition to increasing our income from Raiding, each 1% of Raiding Fervor will also have the following effects:
…
concepts.name: Raiding Fervor

concepts.description: A Country’s Rank is determined by measuring its Prestige relative to other Countries worldwide. It determines what sorts of international activities you are permitted to engage in, what your people and the world expects of you, and where you stand in the global pecking order.…
concepts.name: Rank

concepts.description: An increase or decrease to how fast the Ship is able to act while in battle
concepts.name: Readiness

concepts.description:
A Recognized Power is considered a valid nation-state capable of self-determination by consensus of the Great Powers, which sets them apart from Unrecognized Powers.

An Unrecognized Power may become a Recognized Power by completing the Earning Recognition Journal Entry.
concepts.name: Recognized Power

concepts.description: The percentage of Casualties a Military Unit takes that survive, in some cases by becoming Dependents. Can be increased with Mobilization Options. Recovery Rate is countered by the enemy Military Unit's Kill Rate.
concepts.name: Recovery Rate

concepts.description: Forces the target to change their Government to one similar to the enforcer, and to immediately enact up to … Laws favored by the new regime.
concepts.name: Regime Change

concepts.description: A Company can establish a Regional Company HQ in a foreign Country if they have been granted an Investment Company Charter by their own Country. Additionally they need access to the foreign Country via Foreign Investment Rights and an established presence with a small number of Building Levels. The Regional Company HQ acts mostly like a Company HQ, but will use the foreign Country’s Investment Pool to construct additional Building Levels and will reinvest parts of their Dividends directly into their own Country’s Investment Pool.
concepts.name: Regional Company HQ

concepts.description: A portion of the Dividends collected by certain Professions is reinvested into the economy, adding Money to the Investment Pool. The amount added depends on factors such as the Country’s current … as well as its Gross Domestic Product, with inefficiencies in large economies resulting in some of the investment being wasted.
concepts.name: Reinvestment

concepts.description:
A mutual rating of the diplomatic stance between two Countries, ranging from … to ….

Both sides can influence Relations by spending Influence on the …, …, and … Diplomatic Actions

Relations impact which Diplomatic Actions and Pacts are valid for the two Countries, and also impact the likelihood they will accept diplomatic overtures or take your side in a Diplomatic Play
concepts.name: Relations

concepts.description: All Pops have a Religion, which can only change through Conversion. Their Religion affects their Acceptance Status in their Country.
concepts.name: Religion

concepts.description:
Religious Movements are Political Movements pursuing a better life for people of a specific Religion. If this … is the State Religion of a Country, the movement will push a traditionalist agenda. Otherwise, the movement will push for Laws which give their people greater Acceptance, or even attempt a Secession.

If a Religious Movement's Movement Activism exceeds Protesting (…), it will begin to generate Obstinance in States with Supporting Pops.
concepts.name: Religious Movement

concepts.description: A Resource Potential grants the ability to construct and expand a specific Building type in the state, usually a resource industry such as fisheries, mines, or plantations. The maximum Building Level you can expand the Building to is limited either to a fixed amount per resources, or by the State's amount of Arable Land.
concepts.name: Resource Potential

concepts.description: After a Building has Produced Goods, they are sold at the Local Price. The amount of Money made in the sale is the Building's Revenue, the positive factor of its Balance.
concepts.name: Revenue

concepts.description:
Contrary to Secessions, a Revolution will try to annex the entire Country, reshaping it according to their Core Movement Ideology. A Revolution is the result of a Political Movement that has grown too Radical with high Support and Activism. If the Movement starts an uprising, States in which its Supporting Pops are relatively strong will separate from the rest of the Country and start a Diplomatic Play to annex the Loyalists.

You can lower the Movement’s Activism by reducing the number of Radicals in the Supporting Pops and increasing the Approval of their Interest Groups. You can also weaken and slow a Revolution down using the … Institution.
concepts.name: Revolution

concepts.description: The Risk of a particular Terrain type influences the amount of Casualties and Wounded a Battle would result in.
concepts.name: Risk

concepts.description: A Diplomatic Pact established by one Country targeting another of similar Rank, and which generates Influence for the Country declaring the rivalry. The two Countries must have overlapping Interests to be valid rivals. The Pact will also limit the range of Relations that can be established between the two Countries for as long as the Pact is active.
concepts.name: Rivalry

concepts.description:
Roles determine what areas of your Country a particular Character has influence over. A Character can have one or several Roles.

The list of Roles are: 
   • Ruler (usually also a Politician)
• Heir
• Politician
• Executive
• Agitator
• General
• Admiral
concepts.name: Role

concepts.description: A Ruler is usually the Head of State who represents the Country’s in domestic and world affairs. A Ruler's Character Traits affects the Country directly. When a Ruler dies a new one will take their place, either an Heir if one exists or another Character depending on Government Type.
concepts.name: Ruler

concepts.description:
Rumelian Integrity represents the stability of Ottoman in the … Strategic Region under threat of Secessionist Political Movements. Integrity is tracked in the Great Eastern Crisis Journal Entry.

Movement Activism for all Secessionist Political Movements in Ottoman Empire must be below 75 for Integrity to increase.

The following conditions increase Rumelian Integrity: 
• Legitimacy in Ottoman Empire is 50 or above
• Ottoman Empire is not at War
• Ottoman Empire does not have any growing Secessionist Political Movements
• Ottoman Empire has recently crushed a Secession
concepts.name: Rumelian Integrity

concepts.description:
Russian Aid is support from Russia to our tribes, as fellow brethren of the Orthodox Church. 

The base amount we receive depends on our Relations with Russia: 

• Neutral Relations (or worse): 200 
• Cordial Relations : 400 
• Amicable Relations : 700 
• Friendly Relations : 1000
concepts.name: Russian Aid

concepts.description: A type of … that form the Ship Crew of a Ship.
concepts.name: Sailor

concepts.description: Screening is used to counteract the effects of Vulnerability, a higher Screening value ensures that Ships with higher Vulnerability are less likely to be chosen as a target.
concepts.name: Screening

concepts.description: An intersection or point along a naval Shipping Lane representing a part of the ocean. Shipping Lanes always take the shortest travel distance route between two coastal States. For each multiple of the expected travel distance (…), … is added to the shipping cost.
concepts.name: Sea Node

concepts.description:
Contrary to Revolutions, a Secession will split the Country in two where the Secessionists will fight to break loose and form a new nation. A Secession is the result of a Political Movement that has grown too Radical with high Support and Activism. If the Movement starts an uprising, States in which its Supporting Pops are relatively strong will separate from the rest of the Country and start a Diplomatic Play to break loose.

You can lower the Movement’s Activism by reducing the number of Radicals in the Supporting Pops and increasing the Approval of their Interest Groups. You can also weaken and slow a Secession down using the … Institution.
concepts.name: Secession

concepts.description: Secondary Demands are War Goals that will NOT be enforced in a Diplomatic Play if they decide to back down, but can be taken in a Peace Deal or through capitulation if the play escalates into a War. A Secondary Demand that is targeting the leader of the opposing side can be turned into a Primary Demand by spending Diplomatic Maneuvers, though doing so might result in a Diplomatic Incident.
concepts.name: Secondary Demand

concepts.description: The number of orders to sell a Good on the central Market is used in combination with Buy Orders to determine its Market Price. Sell Orders are generated by the production of the Good in each of the Market's States. The higher the Market Access a State has, the closer the number of Sell Orders generated will be to the total production.
concepts.name: Sell Orders

concepts.description: A Senior Partner in a Customs Union gains control of their Junior Partners’ Markets. While the Junior Partners may continue to Trade with other Markets, only the Senior Partner may issue Embargoes and control Tariff levels. In exchange the Senior Partner shares a minor portion of the Market's Tariff income, while both Countries’ Industries benefit from participating in a more powerful and mature Market.
concepts.name: Senior Partner

concepts.description: A Ship is constructed in a shipyard using Ship Construction. They are organized by their Ship Type in Ship Groups. Ships are used to build Interests across the globe and conduct various Naval Missions in a Fleet.
concepts.name: Ship

concepts.description: Reduces any damage that a Ship would receive from an opponent by this value.
concepts.name: Ship Armor

concepts.description: The Ship Complexity of a Ship is determined by the amount of different Ship Modifications it has. The more Ship Modifications a Ship has, the higher its Ship Complexity and the more Ship Construction it will require to be built or repaired.
concepts.name: Ship Complexity

concepts.description: Ship Construction is produced by … and is used to build and repair ships.
concepts.name: Ship Construction

concepts.description: The maximum amount of Ship Construction that can be applied to a single ship per week.
concepts.name: Ship Construction Capacity

concepts.description: Any Ships that have been set to be built, but are currently not using any Ship Construction, are placed in the Queue. Whenever any Ship Construction becomes available, the first Ship in the Queue will start using that Construction and then switch to being Ship Under Construction.
concepts.name: Ship Construction Queue

concepts.description: The amount of Sailors and … on a Ship. The greater the Crew the more Casualties the Ship will be able to deal and take.
concepts.name: Ship Crew

concepts.description: There are three Ship Groups that consist of Ship Types that fill a similar role. The groups are: Capital Ships, Cruisers and Torpedo Craft.
concepts.name: Ship Group

concepts.description: The total Hit Points of a Ship represent its durability and ability to withstand damage in naval combat.
concepts.name: Ship Hit Points

concepts.description: A Ship Modification is an upgrade that can be applied to a Ship to enhance its capabilities. However, adding more Ship Modifications also increases the Ship Complexity of the Ship, which in turn requires more Ship Construction to build or repair the Ship.
concepts.name: Ship Modification

concepts.description: Upgrades the Ship Modifications of a Ship to match the latest version of it's Ship Template.
concepts.name: Ship Retrofit

concepts.description: An increase or decrease to the movement speed of ships. The slowest ship in a Fleet determines the speed of the entire fleet
concepts.name: Ship Speed

concepts.description: A Ship Template determines the strategic setup for Ships of a certain Ship Type. Ship Modifications modify and govern what values a … ends up having.
concepts.name: Ship Template

concepts.description: Every Ship has a Ship Type that has certain attributes and functions, which make it better or worse for certain Naval Missions.
concepts.name: Ship Type

concepts.description: When a Ship is using Ship Construction it is considered being Under Construction.
concepts.name: Ship Under Construction

concepts.description: The weekly Ship Upkeep represents the cost of Goods required for maintaining a Ship. Upkeep is changed by … if the Ship is docked at an HQ.
concepts.name: Ship Upkeep

concepts.description:
A Shipping Lane is a naval connection of … between two coastal States that is established to either move Goods from place to place as part of a Treaty or to Supply Formations overseas.

A Shipping Lane can be either a Supply Route, a Port Connection or a … Treaty and is reliant on its Shipping Lane Effectiveness to work, provided that its shipping cost is sufficiently covered.
concepts.name: Shipping Lane

concepts.description: The Effectiveness of a Shipping Lane is determined by the strength of a Country’s Supply Network. When Effectiveness is below 100%, the function of the Shipping Lane is reduced to match.
concepts.name: Shipping Lane Effectiveness

concepts.description:
If the supply for a Good is less than … of its demand, that Good is considered to be in Shortage. While in Shortage, different penalties might apply depending on how the Good is used.

Goods used as Input Goods in Buildings will result in an increasing output penalty depending on the severity of the Input Goods Shortage.

In the case of the … Need, a Shortage will affect the Food Security in that State, potentially leading to Starvation and even Famine. … Shortages are based on the Shortage level for each of the individual Goods that fulfill it.

Shortages are usually caused by insufficient availability of the Good in the Market in question, but may also be a result of low Market Access in the relevant State.
concepts.name: Shortage

concepts.description: A practice where one person is permitted legal ownership over another. … will be substituted for other Pops in different Building types based on the Country’s Laws. Laws also determine how existing Pops become Enslaved and how Slaves are uprooted and transported to the Country.
concepts.name: Slavery

concepts.description: Each Pop belongs to a Social Class, and each Social Class belongs to the Lower Strata, Middle Strata, or Upper Strata. A Pop’s Social Class is determined by the Country’s Social Hierarchy.
concepts.name: Social Class

concepts.description:
A Social Hierarchy is comprised of two or more Social Classes. All Pops belong to a Social Hierarchy.

Any Pops not targeted by a country-specific Social Hierarchy are organized into the Base Hierarchy's Lower Class, Middle Class, and Upper Class based on Profession and which correspond to the Lower Strata, Middle Strata, and Upper Strata respectively.

Social Classes for country-specific Social Hierarchies may be determined by factors such as Profession, Culture, and Religion.
concepts.name: Social Hierarchy

concepts.description: A Country’s right to self-govern. When one Country violates the Sovereignty of another they openly disrespect this right. Should the other not respond in turn with an immediate military response enforcing the integrity of their borders, they submit to the violator and permit them military access through their territory.
concepts.name: Sovereignty

concepts.description:
These are Military Units that are not … which are considered Default Units.

Special Units for Armies:
   …
   …
concepts.name: Special Unit

concepts.description: A State Region split into multiple smaller States belonging to different Countries. When split, a portion of the Resource Potentials, Buildings, and Pops are redistributed between the States. Should one Country take control of more than one part of the Split State, these will be combined into a single State.
concepts.name: Split State

concepts.description: Stalled Enactment indicates the percentage chance that the enactment process of a Law will be substantially hindered at the next checkpoint. Its base chance is equal to the total Clout of opposing Interest Groups whose Approval is Unhappy or Angry.
concepts.name: Stalled Enactment

concepts.description: Standard of Living measures a Pop’s living conditions, with their material Wealth as the baseline. It governs Birth Rate and Mortality, and every time it changes it can cause Pops to become more Radical or Loyal. The average Standard of Living in a State affects its Migration Attraction.
concepts.name: Standard of Living

concepts.description:
A Pop is considered to be Starving if their Food Security is too low. This can be due to the Pop's Wealth being too low or simply because there is not enough … the Pop can access.

Mild Starvation begins at … Food Security and has reduced effects.
…

Severe Starvation happens at … Food Security and has harsher effects. If not addressed this will result in the Pop dying.
…

Additionally, Pops suffering from Starvation will also Radicalize over time. How many people Radicalize and at what rate depends on how low their Food Security is.
concepts.name: Starvation

concepts.description: A geographic region controlled by a Country. Pops live and work in the Buildings in the State. Unless it is a Split State its territory is equivalent to a State Region. Unless it is Isolated, it will trade any Goods locally Consumed and Produced with other States in the same Market in to a degree based on its Market Access.
concepts.name: State

concepts.description: A part of the world corresponding with a certain fixed set of Provinces. A State Region is usually equivalent to a State. In certain cases a State Region can become a Split State, where two or more Countries each hold a State in the same State Region.
concepts.name: State Region

concepts.description: The Religion most associated with a Country. It is typically the dominant Religion adhered to by most of its Pops, but can sometimes be legally declared or simply the Religion preferred by its Ruler. It does not typically change.…
concepts.name: State Religion

concepts.description:
A narrow water passage with two connecting Provinces, one on either side of the Strait. A Country only needs control over one of the Provinces in order to be able to manage whose ships have Strait Access through the Strait.
The Strait of Gibraltar requires a Country to control both Provinces to manage the Strait Access rights.
concepts.name: Strait

concepts.description:
Strait Access determines what Ships can pass through a Strait. It can be changed by the Strait Controller of either side of the Strait by setting restrictions. Countries can also secure a Treaty to be guaranteed Strait Access when they would normally be forbidden to pass.

A Strait can be:
Open - All Ships may pass
No Military - Only … Ships & Supply Ships may pass
Closed - No Ships may pass, potentially restricting access to the World Market

Which Countries are affected by this restriction is determined by the Allowed Countries. In the case where the two States have set different Strait Accesses, the most severe Access restriction will take precedence.
concepts.name: Strait Access

concepts.description:
Strait Control is determined by control of the two States on each side of a Strait. In all cases each Country with control over one of the States becomes a Strait Controller that can change the Strait Access through the Strait, with the exception of Strait of Gibraltar which requires control of both States to be able to set the Strait Access to Closed.

In the case where the two States have set different Strait Accesses, the most severe Access restriction will take precedence.
concepts.name: Strait Control

concepts.description:
Strategic Adjacency is an adjacency check for two Countries that is used to allow certain interactions between them if they fulfill the conditions. Two Countries count as Strategically Adjacent if one of these conditions is fulfilled:
• They share a direct border
• They share a direct border with only one Sea Node between them
• One Country is bordering a Subject of the other
• One Country’s Subject is bordering the other Country’s Subject
• One Country is bordering an unpressed War Goal
concepts.name: Strategic Adjacency

concepts.description: AI-controlled Countries will have a Strategic Desire towards Countries they deem geopolitically relevant. Their Strategic Desire represents their overarching diplomatic ambitions towards a Country and is the most important factor in determining their Attitude.
concepts.name: Strategic Desire

concepts.description:
A Strategic Objective can be assigned to an Army. If an enemy or friendly State is assigned as an Army’s Strategic Objective, any of the Army’s advancing Generals will try to advance the Front towards that State. If the State is under friendly control, they will prioritize expanding the defensive perimiter around the State. While defending Generals will focus on the defence of the State and surrounding areas, prioritizing defensive Battles closest to the Strategic Objective.

An Army can have one Strategic Objective, but several Armies can have the same State as their Objective.
concepts.name: Strategic Objective

concepts.description:
A collection of State Regions considered a region of strategic importance. Countries have an Interest in all Regions where they have generated sufficient Involvement.

Maintaining a high enough Interest Tier in a Strategic Region is a prerequisite to participate in Diplomatic Plays taking place there.
concepts.name: Strategic Region

concepts.description: AI-controlled Countries have a set of three Strategies in areas corresponding with the Capacities which govern their long- and short-term goals, and how they will proceed when making decisions in regards to other Countries. Which Strategies are selected is influenced by a number of factors such as the Country's size and Rank, as well as its current Government.
concepts.name: Strategy

concepts.description:
A Country whose Autonomy and right to self-determination is limited to varying degree by an Overlord. Subject relationships are a type of Diplomatic Pact that Countries can be asked to join or forced into with a Diplomatic Play. The precise effects depends on the Subject Type, but tend to include being forced into their Overlord's Market, having to give up a part of their Treasury’s income, decreased Prestige, the inability to start your own Diplomatic Plays or freely decide which side to support in them, and inheriting the Overlord's Ruler as your Head of State.

Subjects can be liberated with a Diplomatic Play started by themselves or a third party. Some Subject types can also be targeted by a Play by their Overlord to reduce their Autonomy further, or even become fully Annexed by them.
concepts.name: Subject

concepts.description: A type of Diplomatic Action that Subjects can issue against their Overlord.
concepts.name: Subject Action

concepts.description:
There are a total of … different Subject Types:
…
See the Subject Types Table on the Diplomacy panel for more in-depth details on the effects of each type.
concepts.name: Subject Type

concepts.description: A Subsidized Building is guaranteed by the Country’s Government to be funded enough to always by able to pay at least the Subsidized Wage. If the building cannot pay its employees according to this rate or higher, and/or if its cost of buying Input Goods exceeds its Revenue from selling Output Goods, the Treasury will cover the difference. This guarantees the Building can hire as many employees as it wants in order to maximize Throughput without concern for how financially viable that is.
concepts.name: Subsidies

concepts.description: When a Subsidized Building cannot pay their Workforce at least the Normal Wage, the remainder is covered by government Subsidies through the Treasury. In return the Building will never fire its Workforce and aim to keep Throughput maximized at all times.
concepts.name: Subsidized Wage

concepts.description: A set of Buildings that perform low-intensity, decentralized production of food and basic resource Goods suitable for mere survival. Their production is split between a small quantity of Goods to be sold on the Market and Subsistence Output used to sustain the meager Standard of Living of the … who work there. They are considerably less effective than most Buildings, but will operate on any unclaimed Arable Land and does not require manual Construction.
concepts.name: Subsistence Building

concepts.description: A form of in-kind income that … generate from Subsistence Farming, which represents the work they perform producing Goods to cover their own Needs. Unlike Wages, Subsistence Output is not paid out from the Building's Revenue and is not subject to Income Taxes.
concepts.name: Subsistence Output

concepts.description: Subventions are a sum of money a Country can pay out to a … for each Imported or Exported Good. Therefore, they will make it more attractive to conduct Trade of a particular good, for example to weaken the competition. A Country’s Laws determines their maximum level of Subventions. The level of Subventions for all members of a Market are determined by the Market Owner.
concepts.name: Subventions

concepts.description: How many Sunken Ships a Fleet has suffered in battle.
concepts.name: Sunken Ships

concepts.description:
The Supply of a Formation determines how quickly Military Units regain Organization.

Supply is usually 100%, but can be lower if an Army is:
- Overseas and supplied by a compromised Shipping Lane
- Will be zero if the Army is completely cut off from its HQ

Modifiers can also apply in some cases.
concepts.name: Supply

concepts.description: An increase or decrease to the maximum amount of supplies a Ship can carry
concepts.name: Supply Capacity

concepts.description: How efficiently a ship uses its supplies. Higher efficiency means lower supply consumption.
concepts.name: Supply Efficiency

concepts.description: Every seafaring Country requires … on the Market to maintain the transportation needs of their Shipping Lanes. The total strength of your Supply Network is determined by comparing the … supply to the total demand across all your Shipping Lanes. This strength is the baseline Effectiveness of all your Shipping Lanes.
concepts.name: Supply Network

concepts.description:
A Formation’s Supply Priority determines the order in which it receives Supply Ships.

Supply Ships will be distributed until all highest level Priority Fleets and Armies have their demand met, after which the distribution will continue on to lower Priority Fleets and Armies.
concepts.name: Supply Priority

concepts.description: A Shipping Lane that supplies a General Ordered to advance or defend a Front only accessible by sea. The General's Supply level is equal to the Supply Route's Effectiveness.
concepts.name: Supply Route

concepts.description:
Supply Ships are used to deliver supplies, rations and ammo to Fleets that are at sea and Armies that are overseas.

They are constructed in a Shipyards much like regular Ships and are retained in a pool unless currently needed.
concepts.name: Supply Ship

concepts.description: A Suppressed Political Movement is less attractive for Pops to support. Your base Suppression ability is determined by your … Law. Suppressing Interest Groups cost Authority.
concepts.name: Suppress

concepts.description: The Initiator or Target in a Diplomatic Play can attempt to Sway any other Country with a high enough Interest Tier in the Strategic Region to their side, by offering a War Goal or other promise such as an Obligation. Attempting to Sway a Country costs Maneuvers, and the chance an AI Country will accept the offer depends on your Relations and their Attitude to you as well as your opponent.
concepts.name: Sway

concepts.description: All AI-controlled Countries involved in a Diplomatic Play begin the play with a level of Sympathy for each side, which influences how likely they are to support that side in the conflict. AI Countries tend to have higher Sympathy for the Target, for countries they have Diplomatic Pacts with, and for those are opposing a Country with high Infamy. Sympathy can also increase over the course of the Diplomatic Play, as a side that gains powerful backers or accrues Infamy through adding War Goals tends to generate Sympathy for the opposing side.
concepts.name: Sympathy

concepts.description: A Religion can be have a Taboo against specific Goods. Pops of that Religion will spend significantly less on Goods they consider Taboo compared to other Goods in the same Pop Needs category.
concepts.name: Taboo

concepts.description: The Country targeted by a Diplomatic Play.
concepts.name: Target

concepts.description: Tariffs are a fee that Countries can collect from a … for each Imported or Exported Good. Therefore, they will make it less attractive to conduct Trade of a particular Good, for example to ensure critical military Goods remain in the Country. A Country’s Laws determines their maximum level of Tariffs. The level of Tariffs for all members of a Market are determined by the Market Owner.
concepts.name: Tariffs

concepts.description: The amount of Taxes collected that are wasted, due to inefficiencies or corruption, prior to entering the government coffers. This is often caused by a Bureaucracy deficit.
concepts.name: Tax Waste

concepts.description: Each point of Taxation Capacity in a State allows for the efficient taxation of … Pops. If the population of a State outgrows its Taxation Capacity, the efficiency of all forms of taxation will be reduced. Taxation Capacity can be increased through researching certain Society Technologies or constructing … Buildings in the State.
concepts.name: Taxation Capacity

concepts.description: Countries can tap into their market economies in various ways. The most common is to tax its populace's private sector incomes, or charge duties on the sales, purchase, or trade of Goods.
concepts.name: Taxes

concepts.description:
Technology covers all innovation in the fields of Production, Military, and Society. Technologies have nation-wide effects, which can range from changing the Country’s operating parameters via Modifiers to unlocking new Production Methods, Buildings, Laws, Decrees, and Diplomatic Pacts.

Progress is made towards new Technologies through Innovation, which is primarily produced by … Buildings. In addition to progress from Innovation, Technologies may propagate from Countries who already have them to those who do not via Technology Spread.

The amount of progress required in a Technology to acquire it depends on its Era. If you have not yet acquired all Technologies from previous Eras, the amount required will increase further.
concepts.name: Technology

concepts.description:
Technology Eras are a rough classification of which time period a certain idea was first discovered or developed.

Era I inventions were well-known in many parts of the world prior to 1836.
Era II inventions are associated with the First Industrial Revolution (1836 to mid-19th century).
Era III is a period of evolution, stabilization, and standardization that runs until late 19th century.
Era IV corresponds with the Second Industrial Revolution around the turn of the century.
Era V inventions are transformative, modern ideas.

Technologies require more Innovation to discover the later Era it appears in. If you have not yet acquired all Technologies from previous Eras, the amount required will increase further.
concepts.name: Technology Era

concepts.description: One Technology that you have not yet acquired from each category (Production, Military, and Society) is always spreading to you from Countries that have acquired them. The progress you get in spreading Technologies is randomized each week around a base value depending on your Country's Literacy. If no Country has invented a certain Technology yet it cannot spread to you, so you are more likely to acquire early Era Technologies from Technology Spread than later ones.
concepts.name: Technology Spread

concepts.description:
How strained the relationship is between a Colonizing Country and nearby Decentralized Nations. Tensions rise with all nearby Decentralized Nations whenever a Province is taken over, and decreases over time as long as no new land is taken.

If the tension level rises to Volatile, continued colonization may trigger a Native Uprising.
concepts.name: Tension

concepts.description:
A Province’s Terrain determines its Combat Width and how volatile and unpredictable Battles in that Province is. Generals can also be more or less versed in fighting in different types of Terrain.

The Terrain of a given Province can change as a result of the Buildings constructed in the State.
concepts.name: Terrain

concepts.description: A Terrain Label is a grouping of several Terrain Types. Character Traits can have Modifiers affecting all Terrain Types with a specific Terrain Label.
concepts.name: Terrain Labels

concepts.description: A region of adjacent Provinces under the control of a single Country. Fronts are created on the border between two Theaters controlled by Countries hostile to each other in a War or Diplomatic Play.
concepts.name: Theater

concepts.description: The effectiveness of the Workforce of a Building. Throughput increases both the Input Goods and the Output Goods or other effects. It can increase as a result of Economy of Scale, and might be adjusted up or down due to Modifiers.
concepts.name: Throughput

concepts.description: A Modifier with an expiry date, after which it will disappear. Timed Modifiers can either maintain its full effect up until its expiry date, or Decay gradually until the date has been reached.
concepts.name: Timed Modifier

concepts.description: Notifications that appear one at a time in the middle of the screen.
concepts.name: Toast

concepts.description: Tolls can be raised by Countries that Control a Strait. They add a cost that is a share of the Trade going through them. This cost is covered by the affected … and reduces their profitability, while the Country controlling the Strait gains additional income from this. Tolls can be raised individually by both controllers of a Strait and are summed up.
concepts.name: Tolls

concepts.description:
Tomas Zumalakarregi Imatz

Born on December 29th 1788 in Ormaiztegi, Gipuzkoa
Died on June 24th 1835 in Zegama, Gipuzkoa

Tomás de Zumalacárregui e Imaz, also referred to as \"Uncle Tomas\" by his soldiers, was a Basque military officer and as Captain General of the Carlist forces in Navarra and the Basque Country responsible for the organization of the army as well as decisive early victories for the Carlist cause.
His sudden death on account of a gunshot wound in the field in the early summer of 1835 resulted in a considerable setback for Don Carlos' ambitions.
concepts.name: Tomás de Zumalacárregui

concepts.description: Trade is the process of Importing and Exporting Goods. Most Trade is conducted autonomously by a … via the World Market, but Countries can also set up Treaties to trade Goods between them directly. Trade can be an effective way for Countries to improve their economic situation.
concepts.name: Trade

concepts.description: Trade Advantage is the value that determines the Import Price and Export Price for a particular … and therefore also directly affects the amount of Goods traded. It is influenced by factors such as the … level, the Market Area’s share of global production of a Good, Interests in relevant Strategic Regions and Trade Privileges. Trade Advantage is calculated per Good, per direction, so the Trade Advantage differs for Importing Coal and Exporting Fabric for example.
concepts.name: Trade Advantage

concepts.description: Trade Capacity is generated by … levels and used to conduct Trade with the World Market. The quantity of Goods traded per Trade Capacity varies per Good.
concepts.name: Trade Capacity

concepts.description:
Trade Potential is a rough approximation for the potential to Import or Export a Good in a particular State. It considers numerous factors such as the the Local Price, the World Market Price, Trade Advantage, the difference between Production and Consumption, as well as Tariffs and Subventions. 

Trade Potential should not be considered an accurate predictor of trade volumes, but is useful to determine which Goods a State is likely to Trade more of if it has free Trade Capacity.
concepts.name: Trade Potential

concepts.description: A type of Treaty Article granted by one Market Owner to another. It affects every Country in the receiver's Market, increasing their Trade Advantage relative to how much of the Trade is conducted with the giver's Market.
concepts.name: Trade Privilege

concepts.description: Trade generates revenue for the … managing it, depending on the Market Price difference and the volume traded. Tariffs reduce the Trade Revenue generated.
concepts.name: Trade Revenue

concepts.description: The amount of a Good that is Imported or Exported with each Trade Capacity used.
concepts.name: Traded Quantity

concepts.description: Tradition Traits are rites, ideas and customs that Cultures might hold or pick up on over time that can be recognizable despite very distinct Heritages or Languages. Contrary to Heritage and Language Traits, Traditions do not belong to any Trait Group.
concepts.name: Tradition Trait

concepts.description: The Training Rate is the amount of Manpower that can be trained per week at a Military Building.
concepts.name: Training Rate

concepts.description: The Transfer of Power determines how a Ruler’s power is given to the next Ruler and when this transfer will take place.
concepts.name: Transfer of Power

concepts.description: The Treasury keeps track of your Country’s assets. Each week your budget balance will result in the Treasury taking out more Loans to cover a Money deficit, or depositing Money into the Gold Reserves.
concepts.name: Treasury

concepts.description: Money collected from or remitted to the other Country in a Treaty.
concepts.name: Treaties

concepts.description:
A Treaty is a type of bilateral agreement between two Countries and is made up of individual Articles that define the rights, duties and Influence cost of each Country. Treaties remain in effect until either side breaks the agreement or withdraws from it after the initial Binding Period has passed.

Treaties may also be Forced upon a Country in the form of War Reparations as a result of a Diplomatic Play.
concepts.name: Treaty

concepts.description:
A coastal Split State held under a Treaty for the purpose of opening Trade with another Country. A Treaty Port is part of the Market of the Country that ceded the Province, and can freely Trade with the World Market.

Tariffs, Subventions and Embargoes do not affect Treaty Ports, and the owner gets Trade Advantage when importing Goods exported by the Treaty Port (and vice versa). If the Treaty ceding the Treaty Port, is broken, it ceases to be a Treaty Port and becomes a regular State.
concepts.name: Treaty Port

concepts.description: Unrecognized Powers may turn a weaker Country into their Tributary (Subject). A Tributary is a more autonomous Subject Type that are able to start their own Diplomatic Plays and are not forced to join their Overlord’s Wars. They must pay 20% of their Treasury income to their Overlord each week.
concepts.name: Tributary

concepts.description: A Truce is a diplomatic status where one Country is prevented from making a Diplomatic Demand or joining in an offensive Diplomatic Play against another Country. Truces may be unilateral or bilateral, and are created in a variety of ways, such as when a Peace Deal is signed or an Alliance is broken.
concepts.name: Truce

concepts.description:
States and Cultures with Turmoil contain Radicals that are unhappy with their current circumstances. The amount of Turmoil is equal to the fraction of the State's or Culture's Workforce that are Radical.

Turmoil can inflict a number of negative local status effects on a State if it gets high enough. Cultural Turmoil can impact a whole Country in very disruptive ways.
concepts.name: Turmoil

concepts.description: A Country’s Unclaimed Leverage is the Leverage that no Power Bloc has claimed on that Country. It is based on the Country’s Leverage Resistance which in turn is based on a number of factors like their Laws and Population, more people means more people to convince.
concepts.name: Unclaimed Leverage

concepts.description: When a Building is using Construction it is considered being Under Construction.
concepts.name: Under Construction

concepts.description:
An Unemployed Pop does not work in any of its State’s Buildings and therefore does not collect a Wage. They are likely to take the next best job that comes along, and will likely Emigrate if nothing comes along.

Pops living in a state will face an increasing penalty to Birth Rate proportional to the unemployement rate in that state, up to the following:
…
concepts.name: Unemployed

concepts.description: A Unification Candidate is a Country considered a viable candidate for unification. The conditions for who qualifies as a Unification Candidate varies depending on which unified nation it is.
concepts.name: Unification Candidate

concepts.description: A Unification Supporter is a Country that favors a particular Unification Candidate. Should the unification be successful, the Unification Supporter will become a part of the union.
concepts.name: Unification Supporter

concepts.description:
A State that is within a Country’s domain, but considered a territorial holding or frontier beyond the reach of Institutions and Government. Pops who live in Unincorporated States are disenfranchised and do not contribute much Political Strength to their Interest Groups, nor can they Vote in Elections. On the upside (for them) they are exempt from Taxation.

Unincorporated States do not cost Bureaucracy to maintain, as Taxes are not collected and Institutions do not provide any benefits there. Unincorporated States can be Incorporated, which will put it under the direct management of the Country’s central authority.…
concepts.name: Unincorporated State

concepts.description: Each Unit under recruitment either has a level of a Military Building in the Construction Queue or have a Military Building that are trying to hire Pops in order to be able to create the Military Unit.
concepts.name: Units under Recruitment

concepts.description: Unrealized Taxes is the amount of Taxes that the Country is failing to collect due to various reasons, including but not limited to insufficient Taxation Capacity and Tax Waste.
concepts.name: Unrealized Taxes

concepts.description: Unrecognized Powers are Polities perceived as inferior and uncivilized by the reigning Great Powers, who regard them as little more than potential future conquests. As a result their Prestige is penalized and they can be targeted with more severe Diplomatic Plays. They are also restricted in what Ranks they may reach, no matter how much Prestige they acquire.…
concepts.name: Unrecognized Power

concepts.description:
The Upper Strata consist of Pops with Professions they Qualify for mostly on the basis of Wealth. These Professions are typically not available to Pops that have low Acceptance either. They tend to hold Pop Ownership Shares in their Buildings and draw Dividends and collect Interest in addition to Wages.

Which Pops belong to this Strata depends on the Country’s Social Hierarchy.
concepts.name: Upper Strata

concepts.description: Urbanization is generated by most Buildings constructed in a State to varying degrees. When sufficient Urbanization has accumulated in a State, an … will be automatically expanded.
concepts.name: Urbanization

concepts.description: Unrecognized Powers may turn a weaker Country into their Vassal (Subject). A Vassal is a Subject Type that cannot start their own Diplomatic Plays yet are forced to join their Overlord’s Wars, and must also pay 30% of their Treasury income to their Overlord each week.
concepts.name: Vassal

concepts.description: Military Units and the Crew in Ships gain Veterancy Ranks by earning Experience. Higher Ranks grant increasing bonuses to the offensive and defensive capabilities of the Military Unit or Ship in question.
concepts.name: Veterancy Rank

concepts.description:
An increase or decrease to how hard to detect the Ship is

A Fleet’s Detection and the enemies Visibility are used in conjunction to determine the chance to spawn a Naval Battle and how many Ships will be involved.
concepts.name: Visibility

concepts.description: Your Laws determine whether any given Pop gets to cast a Vote, and if so, how much Political Strength that … will count for. Votes are cast for Parties during Election periods. Pops will tend to vote for the Party their Interest Group belongs to, but may be won over by another Party with greater Momentum. After the Election date, the number of total Votes each Party received will be fixed until the next Election, and will increase the Clout of any Interest Groups that are members of the Party.
concepts.name: Votes

concepts.description: Higher Vulnerability Ships are more likely to be chosen as a target by enemy Ships unless the Fleet has sufficient Screening to protect all of its Ships.
concepts.name: Vulnerability

concepts.description:
Wages paid to Pops by the Building they work in depends on several factors, the most prominent being the Pop's Profession and the Building's financial situation. If a Building's Balance allows for raising Wages at all, the Building will only do so if it needs to in order to attract more Pops to its Workforce. If a Building's Balance is negative, it will consider lowering Wages to return to profitability.

You can guarantee that the Workforce is paid a competitive Wage by Subsidizing the building. This will keep it afloat with funds from the Treasury if necessary.
concepts.name: Wage

concepts.description: Pops in the employ of a Country’s Government Buildings and Military Buildings get paid Wages from the Treasury each week, according to the Government Wage and Military Wage respectively.
concepts.name: Wages

concepts.description: An active armed conflict between two sides of co-belligerent Countries as a result of the failure to peacefully resolve a Diplomatic Play. During Wars, Commanders on land and at sea will follow Orders to complete certain objectives, often resulting in Battles between the two sides.
concepts.name: War

concepts.description:
A Population tends to suffer while their Country is at War. The following factors contribute to War Exhaustion:

* how much Land has been Occupied
* how many War Goals the enemy controls
* how many Casualties have been taken
* how much the Country is suffering from Turmoil

War Exhaustion reduces War Support each week, bringing the Country closer to agreeing to a Peace Deal.
concepts.name: War Exhaustion

concepts.description:
War Goals are the objectives a Country is fighting a War over. They are determined during the Diplomatic Play and are fixed after the War has begun. Each War Goal claimed in a Peace Deal decreases the chance the opponent will accept it, and increases the degree by which their War Support must be Exhausted before they will agree. War Support can only drop below 0 if the opposing side Controls all their War Goals.

The first War Goal claimed as part of the Diplomatic Play is considered your Primary Demand, and some Diplomatic Plays require it to be included in all Peace Deals.
concepts.name: War Goal

concepts.description: One Country on each side of a War is considered the War Leader for that side, usually (but not always) corresponding to the Initiator and Target of the Diplomatic Play that spawned it. They are the only ones who may propose Peace Deals, though every Peace Deal must be ratified by all negotiating members of the War to be accepted.
concepts.name: War Leader

concepts.description: A secondary War Goal that can be added onto a Diplomatic Play by choosing a specific Article to accompany it and claimed as part of a Peace Deal. If enforced, a new Treaty will be created containing all Articles that were selected as war reparations by the other Country with a minimum binding period that lasts for the duration of the Truce.
concepts.name: War Reparations

concepts.description: A measure of how eager your Country’s population is to remain in a War. Positive values indicate a desire to stay in the War while negative values indicate a general opposition to it. Once War Support reaches … the Country will immediately capitulate, allowing all War Goals to be pressed on them. War Support can only drop below 0 if the opposing side Controls all their War Goals.
concepts.name: War Support

concepts.description:
A measure of a Pop’s material assets. To sustain a certain level of Wealth the Pop has a set of Needs it must satisfy each week. If their Income does not cover the cost of these Needs, their Wealth will eventually decrease. If they have Money left over after purchasing the necessary Goods, Wealth will soon increase.

Wealth is the main factor contributing to a Pop's Standard of Living, and under certain Laws it may affect other aspects of their life such as Literacy and Voting Rights.
concepts.name: Wealth

concepts.description: Welfare Payments are a form of direct subsidy paid by by a Country to all Pops in the Workforce that receive wages lower than the defined fraction of the Normal Wage.
concepts.name: Welfare Payments

concepts.description: How many Ships have Withdrawn from the battle.
concepts.name: Withdrawn Ships

concepts.description: The Workforce of a Building consists of Pops of different Professions depending on the currently active Production Methods.
concepts.name: Workforce

concepts.description: The part of a Pop that make up the Workforce that work in Buildings for Wages. They are the main source of a Pop's Income and Political Strength.
concepts.name: Working Adults

concepts.description: The World Market serves as the place to conduct autonomous Trade. The price of Goods is determined by the number of Imports and Exports. States need Market Access in order to conduct Trade via their …. Landlocked Countries can get Transit Rights from other Countries to secure access to the World Market.
concepts.name: World Market

concepts.description: World Market Access exists if a State is connected to the World Market via a World Market Hub. Its value is impacted by the State’s Market Access.
concepts.name: World Market Access

concepts.description: A World Market Hub is the place from which Trade via the World Market is conducted. It is created if a Market Area has at least one …. The location of a World Market Hub can change depending on … levels and State’s Gross Domestic Product.
concepts.name: World Market Hub

concepts.description: The average price at which a Good is traded on the World Market. This is dependent on the number of Exports versus Imports of that Good.
concepts.name: World Market Price

concepts.description: Casualties that are merely Wounded in Battle or due to Attrition. Some Wounded Casualties recover and return to active service after some time, while others end up as Dependents of other Pops in your Country.
concepts.name: Wounded

concepts.description:
A Zaibatsu is a family-owned and vertically-integrated industrial and financial conglomerate.

A typical Zaibatsu is organized around a holding company and a bank, which hold ownership shares in several, typically industrial, subsidiary companies. The Zaibatsu emerged from family merchant congolomerates of the late Edo period, which made use of their pre-existing wealth and ties to the state to consolidate control of much of Japan's industrial base.

Companies regarded as Zaibatsu include Mitsui, Mitsubishi, Yasuda, and Sumitomo.
concepts.name: Zaibatsu
